definition_en: the central or most important part of something
core_image: 苹果被横切开，正中露出一圈整齐的籽
scene: 老师把苹果横着切开，让学生看中间那一圈小小的籽。The core of an apple holds its seeds in a small room.
sceneCN: 这里 core 指「果核」（第 2 个义项：果实中央装种子的部分）；句意是苹果的果核像一间小屋，装着它的种子。

senses.title: The central part
senses.definition: the central or most important part of something
senses.definitionCN: 某物最中心或最重要的部分
senses.example: The core of the team is its two oldest players.
senses.exampleCN: 这支队伍的核心是两位最年长的球员。
senses.why: Every circle needs a middle before it can have an edge.
senses.whyCN: 每个圆都要先有中心，才能有边缘。

senses.title: The seed chamber of fruit
senses.definition: the hard central part of an apple or pear that holds the seeds
senses.definitionCN: 苹果或梨中间装着种子的硬心
senses.example: Cut the apple and take out the core.
senses.exampleCN: 把苹果切开，取出果核。
senses.why: The fruit builds a small room for its seeds and calls it a core.
senses.whyCN: 果实为种子盖了一间小屋，管它叫果核。

senses.title: The central meaning
senses.definition: the central idea or meaning of an argument or a text
senses.definitionCN: 论点或文章最中心的观点或意思
senses.example: The core of her argument is simple.
senses.exampleCN: 她论点的要点很简单。
senses.why: Strip away the leaves of words and a few hard seeds remain.
senses.whyCN: 剥去话语的枝叶，剩下的就是几粒硬籽。

intro.en: Core comes from Latin cor, heart, whose stem cord- also shapes cordial and concord.
intro.cn: core 来自拉丁语 cor（心），其词干 cord- 也构成了 cordial 与 concord。

items.en: Cor meant heart, and by extension the seat of feeling.
items.cn: cor 意为心，并引申为情感的所在。

items.en: The stem cord- carried the same sense into compounds.
items.cn: 词干 cord- 把同样的意思带进了复合词。

items.en: Old French cors named the heart or the inner body.
items.cn: 古法语 cors 指心脏或身体内部。

items.en: English core first named the inner part of fruit.
items.cn: 英语 core 最初指果实内部的部分。

items.en: It now names the centre of anything, from the earth to an argument.
items.cn: 今天它指任何事物的中心，从地核到论点。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the heart base cor-, and the meaning group names other words for a centre.
note.cn: 形近组共享表示心的词基 cor-，近义组列出其他表示中心与实质的说法。

entries.definition: an organised body of people with one purpose
entries.definitionCN: 为同一目的组织起来的团体

entries.definition: a thick string or thin rope
the light bark of a tree, used for stoppers
entries.definitionCN: 一种轻软的树皮，可做瓶塞

entries.definition: the exact middle of a space
the most important part of a matter
the inner nature that makes a thing what it is
entries.definitionCN: 使事物成其为自身的内在本质

normalIntro.en: These hooks start with a fruit cut open, then move to a team and to the heart of an argument.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从切开的果实开始，再到一支队伍，最后到论点的内核。

normal.en: Cor is Latin for heart, so the core is the heart of anything.
normal.cn: cor 在拉丁语里是心，所以 core 就是任何事物的心。

normal.en: An apple keeps its seeds in the core, as a house keeps its family in one room.
normal.cn: 苹果把种子留在果核里，就像房子把家人留在一间屋里。

normal.en: Cut away everything soft and the core still stands.
normal.cn: 把柔软的部分都切掉，果核还立在那里。

normal.en: A team has a core: the few people the others lean on.
normal.cn: 一支队伍有核心，就是其他人都依靠的那几个人。

normal.en: If you forget the sense, picture the hard middle you never eat.
normal.cn: 如果忘了意思，就想想那个你从不吃的硬心。

abstract.en: Picture a hard stone at the centre of a peach.
abstract.cn: 想象一颗硬核躺在桃子正中。

abstract.en: Picture a wheel whose hub holds every spoke.
abstract.cn: 想象一个轮子，轮毂把所有辐条收拢在一起。

abstract.en: Picture a sentence with all its modifiers peeled away.
abstract.cn: 想象一句话被剥去所有修饰，只剩主干。

examples.en: The core of the city is its old square.
examples.cn: 这座城市的中心是它古老的广场。

examples.en: She cut out the core and sliced the rest.
examples.cn: 她去掉果核，把其余部分切成片。

examples.en: Honesty lies at the core of their friendship.
examples.cn: 诚实是他们友谊的核心。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 core 记成「果心」：苹果正中那圈装着籽的硬心，就是整颗果子的核心。

root: 源自拉丁语 cor（心）及其属格 cordis，本指心脏，后引申为事物最中心的部分。

sensesIntro.en: From the middle of a fruit, to the middle of a room, and at last to the middle of an idea.
sensesIntro.cn: 从果实的正中，到事物的中心，最后到一个想法的内核。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a fruit cut open to show its seed chamber.
core.cn: 核心意象：果实被切开，露出装籽的内室。

branches.en: The middle of a thing draws the eye first.
branches.cn: 事物的正中总是最先吸引目光。

branches.en: Fruit hides its seeds in a hard inner room.
branches.cn: 果实把种子藏在坚硬的内心室里。

branches.en: An argument also has a hard centre that must hold.
branches.cn: 一个论点也有必须立得住的硬核。

branches.en: Both name a physical middle, one abstract and one edible.
branches.cn: 两者都指物理上的中间，一个抽象，一个可食。

branches.en: From fruit to thought, the core is the part that must stay.
branches.cn: 从果实到思想，核心都是必须留下的部分。

intro.en: Core rests on Latin cor, heart, and its stem cord-, which also shapes cordial and concord.
intro.cn: core 建立在拉丁语 cor（心）及其词干 cord- 之上，cordial 与 concord 也由它构成。

latinIntro.en: The heart base cord- still beats inside cordial, concord and discord.
latinIntro.cn: 表示心的词基 cord- 至今仍活在 cordial、concord 与 discord 里。

items.example: Two cores fell into the bowl.

items.meaning: a tool that removes a core
warm and friendly from the heart
items.example: They gave us a cordial welcome.

definition_zh: 角落；街角；拐角；把…逼入绝境
definition_en: the point where two lines or surfaces meet, or to force someone into a place with no escape
core_image: 两面墙相遇，挤出一个九十度的尖角
scene: 小猫被门和墙夹住，退无可退，只好弓起背。The cat was cornered between the door and the wall.
sceneCN: 这里 corner 指「把…逼入绝境」（第 3 个义项：使某人无处可退）；句意是猫被门和墙夹在角落里。

senses.title: An inside angle
senses.definition: the place inside a room where two walls or edges meet
senses.definitionCN: 房间内两堵墙或两条边相接的地方
senses.example: There is an old chair in the corner of the room.
senses.exampleCN: 房间角落里有一把旧椅子。
senses.why: Two walls meet and leave a small pocket that holds what we hide.
senses.whyCN: 两堵墙相接，留下一个小口袋，收藏我们藏起来的东西。

senses.title: The bend of a street
senses.definition: the point where two streets meet
senses.definitionCN: 两条街道相接的地方
senses.example: A small shop stands on the corner.
senses.exampleCN: 街角有一家小商店。
senses.why: A street corner is where one path hands you over to another.
senses.whyCN: 街角是一条路把你交给另一条路的地方。

senses.title: To trap someone
senses.definition: to force a person or animal into a place from which there is no escape
senses.definitionCN: 把人或动物逼到无路可退的地方
senses.example: The dog cornered the cat under the car.
senses.exampleCN: 狗把猫逼到了车底下。
senses.why: A corner has two walls, so the hunted thing has only one way left.
senses.whyCN: 角落有两面墙，被追的东西只剩下一条路。

intro.en: Corner goes back to Latin cornu, a horn or pointed tip, through Old French corniere, a projecting corner.
intro.cn: corner 可追溯到拉丁语 cornu（角、尖头），经古法语 corniere（突出的角）进入英语。

items.en: Cornu meant a horn or any pointed end.
items.cn: cornu 意为兽角或任何尖出的末端。

items.en: The same word named the wing of an army.
items.cn: 同一个词也用来指军队的侧翼。

items.en: Corniere named the projecting corner of a building.
items.cn: corniere 指建筑物向外突出的角。

items.en: English corner first meant a sheltered or hidden angle.
items.cn: 英语 corner 最初指可以遮蔽、藏身的角。

items.en: It now covers room corners, street corners and tight spots with no way out.
items.cn: 今天它涵盖房间的角、街角，以及无路可退的困境。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers short words in -orn or -or, and the meaning group names other kinds of bend and hiding place.
note.cn: 形近组收集以 -orn 或 -or 结尾的短词，近义组列出其他表示转折与藏身处的说法。

entries.definition: an official who investigates sudden deaths
a small brass musical instrument
the grain of a cereal plant
the space between two meeting lines
entries.definitionCN: 两条相交线之间的空间

entries.definition: a small sheltered corner of a room
a place where a road turns

normalIntro.en: These hooks begin with two walls meeting, then move to a street bend and to an animal with no way out.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从两面墙相接开始，再到街道的转弯，最后到无路可退的动物。

normal.en: Corner begins like corn, but it is the sharp end of a wall.
normal.cn: corner 开头像 corn，但它指的是墙的尖角。

normal.en: A corner is where two straight lines decide to meet.
normal.cn: 角落就是两条直线决定相遇的地方。

normal.en: Shops love corners because two streets bring two crowds.
normal.cn: 商店喜欢街角，因为两条街带来两股人流。

normal.en: If someone is cornered, every wall is behind them.
normal.cn: 如果一个人被逼到角落，每面墙都在他身后。

normal.en: Cutting corners saves time now and costs more later.
normal.cn: 偷工减料现在省时间，以后却要付出更多。

abstract.en: Picture a mouse pressed into the angle of two walls.
abstract.cn: 想象一只老鼠被挤进两面墙形成的夹角。

abstract.en: Picture a road that turns and hides what comes next.
abstract.cn: 想象一条路拐了弯，把后面的景象藏起来。

abstract.en: Picture a page folded so that one point creases hard.
abstract.cn: 想象一页纸被折起，有一个点折出硬痕。

examples.en: There is a lamp in the corner of the room.
examples.cn: 房间角落里有一盏灯。

examples.en: We met at the corner of the street.
examples.cn: 我们在街角见了面。

examples.en: The dog cornered the cat under the car.
examples.cn: 狗把猫逼到了车底下。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 corner 记成 corn（谷物）加 er：谷粒堆在仓房最里面的尖角，那就是角落。

root: 源自拉丁语 cornu（角、尖头），经古法语 corniere（突出的角）进入英语，本指突出的尖角，后泛指夹角与街角。

sensesIntro.en: From an angle inside a room, to the bend of a street, and at last to the trap that such an angle makes.
sensesIntro.cn: 从房间内的夹角，到街道的转弯，最后到这种夹角造成的困境。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two walls meeting at a sharp right angle.
core.cn: 核心意象：两面墙以直角相遇，挤出一个尖角。

branches.en: The angle inside a room holds chairs, lamps and hidden things.
branches.cn: 房间里的夹角放着椅子、灯和藏起来的东西。

branches.en: A street corner gathers two flows of people into one point.
branches.cn: 街角把两股人流汇聚到一个点上。

branches.en: To corner is to use walls as a cage.
branches.cn: 逼入绝境，就是把墙当成笼子来用。

branches.en: The same shape that shelters can also trap.
branches.cn: 同一个形状既能遮蔽，也能困住人。

branches.en: A bend in a street can turn into a dead end.
branches.cn: 街道的一个转弯，也可能变成死路。

intro.en: Corner is a base word from Latin cornu, horn, extended by old French endings and modern compounds.
intro.cn: corner 是源自拉丁语 cornu（角）的词根词，又经古法语词尾与现代复合构词扩展。

latinIntro.en: The horn base corn- also appears in corner, cornet and unicorn.
latinIntro.cn: 表示角的词基 corn- 也出现在 corner、cornet 与 unicorn 中。

items.meaning: a pointed meeting of two sides

items.example: The cornered fox turned to fight.
items.exampleCN: 被逼到角落的狐狸转身反抗。

items.meaning: the act of forcing into a corner
items.meaningCN: 把对方逼入角落的行为
items.example: The cornering of the thief took a minute.
items.exampleCN: 把小偷逼进角落用了一分钟。

items.meaning: the first stone of a building
items.example: They laid the cornerstone in May.
items.exampleCN: 他们在五月安放了基石。

items.meaning: a small shop on a street corner
a kick taken from the corner of a field
items.example: He scored from a corner kick.

definition_zh: 公司；法人团体；市政机构
definition_en: a large business company, or a group of people treated by law as a single body
core_image: 许多小人被装进同一个巨大的西装外壳里
scene: 这栋玻璃大楼里坐着几千名员工，门口铜牌上刻着公司的全名。The corporation employs three thousand people in this city.
sceneCN: 这里 corporation 指「公司」（第 1 个义项：依法成立的大型企业）；句意是这家公司在本市雇用了三千人。

pos.zh: 公司；法人团体；市政机构

senses.title: A large business company
senses.definition: a large business organisation that the law treats as a single unit
senses.definitionCN: 法律视为单一整体的大型商业组织
senses.example: She works for a corporation that builds bridges.
senses.exampleCN: 她在一家修桥的公司工作。
senses.why: Hundreds of owners hide behind one legal name.
senses.whyCN: 成百上千位股东藏在一个法律名字后面。

senses.title: A legal body
senses.definition: a group of people given the rights of a single person by law
senses.definitionCN: 被法律赋予单个人权利的一群人
senses.example: The charity was registered as a corporation.
senses.exampleCN: 这家慈善机构被登记为法人团体。
senses.why: Law lends a body to a group so that it can sign and be sued.
senses.whyCN: 法律给一群人一副身体，让它能签约也能被起诉。

senses.title: The rulers of a town
senses.definition: the group of people who govern a town or city
senses.definitionCN: 管理一座城镇或城市的一群人
senses.example: The old town corporation kept the market clean.
senses.exampleCN: 旧时的市政机构负责保持市场整洁。
senses.why: A town also needs one body to speak for many streets.
senses.whyCN: 一座城镇也需要一副身体，替许多街道说话。

intro.en: Corporation comes from Latin corpus, body, through corporatio, a body formed of many members.
intro.cn: corporation 来自拉丁语 corpus（身体），经 corporatio（由许多成员组成的一个身体）而来。

items.en: Corpus meant a body, living or not.
items.cn: corpus 指身体，无论是否有生命。

items.en: Corporare meant to make into one body.
items.cn: corporare 意为使结合成一个身体。

items.en: Corporatio named the joining of members into one whole.
items.cn: corporatio 指成员结合成一个整体。

items.en: English corporation first named a guild or a town body.
items.cn: 英语 corporation 最初指行会或市政团体。

items.en: It now usually means a large company with a legal life of its own.
items.cn: 今天它通常指拥有独立法律生命的大型公司。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the Latin body base corpor-, and the meaning group names other kinds of business body.
note.cn: 形近组共享拉丁语表示身体的词基 corpor-，近义组列出其他表示商业实体的说法。

entries.definition: belonging to a large company
relating to the human body
having a physical body
a business that sells goods or services
entries.definitionCN: 出售商品或服务的商业机构

entries.definition: a business partnership or company
entries.definitionCN: 合伙或股份形式的商行

entries.definition: a commercial enterprise or trade

normalIntro.en: These hooks start with many people sharing one legal body, then move to a charity and to a town government.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从许多人共用一副法律身体开始，再到慈善机构，最后到市政机构。

normal.en: Corpus is Latin for body, so a corporation is a body made of people.
normal.cn: corpus 在拉丁语里是身体，corporation 就是用许多人拼成的一副身体。

normal.en: The company can sign a contract as if it had one hand.
normal.cn: 公司能签合同，仿佛它只有一只手。

normal.en: Shareholders come and go, but the body keeps its name.
normal.cn: 股东来来去去，这副身体却保留自己的名字。

normal.en: Think of a suit so large that a whole office fits inside.
normal.cn: 想象一套大得能装下整个办公室的西装。

normal.en: A corporation is a person invented by lawyers.
normal.cn: 公司是律师发明出来的一种人。

abstract.en: Picture a hundred hands signing one paper.
abstract.cn: 想象一百只手在同一张纸上签字。

abstract.en: Picture a building wearing a name plate like a badge.
abstract.cn: 想象一栋大楼把名牌像徽章一样戴在身上。

abstract.en: Picture a body with windows instead of eyes.
abstract.cn: 想象一副身体，眼睛的位置装着窗户。

examples.en: The corporation opened a new factory last year.
examples.cn: 这家公司去年开了一家新工厂。

examples.en: Large corporations pay a special tax here.
examples.cn: 大型公司在这里要缴一种特别税。

examples.en: The town corporation voted to repair the bridge.
examples.cn: 市政机构投票决定修桥。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 corporation 记成 corpor（身体）加 ation：许多人合成一副身体，就是法人公司。

root: 源自拉丁语 corpus（身体）及其动词 corporare（结成一体），本指由许多成员组成的一个整体，后指法人团体与大型公司。

sensesIntro.en: From a body of members, to a company with legal life, and at last to the body that governs a town.
sensesIntro.cn: 从由成员组成的身体，到有法律生命的公司，最后到管理城镇的机构。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: many small figures packed inside one large suit.
core.cn: 核心意象：许多小人被装进同一套巨大的西装里。

branches.en: A large company acts as one body in the market.
branches.cn: 大型公司在市场上作为一个整体行动。

branches.en: Law gives a group the rights of a single person.
branches.cn: 法律赋予一个团体单个人的权利。

branches.en: A town body speaks for many streets at once.
branches.cn: 市政机构同时替许多街道说话。

branches.en: Both rest on the idea of one legal person made of many.
branches.cn: 两者都建立在许多人合成一个法律人的观念上。

branches.en: A charity and a town council share the same legal shape.
branches.cn: 慈善机构与市政机构共享同一种法律形态。

intro.en: Corporation joins Latin corpus, body, with the noun ending -ation, meaning a body formed from members.
intro.cn: corporation 由拉丁语 corpus（身体）加名词词尾 -ation 构成，意为由成员组成的身体。

latinIntro.en: The body base corpor- also runs through corporate, incorporate and corpse.
latinIntro.cn: 表示身体的词基 corpor- 也贯穿 corporate、incorporate 与 corpse。

items.meaning: of a body or a company
items.exampleCN: 这座塔楼里全是公司办公室。

items.example: They corporately agreed to the plan.
items.exampleCN: 他们以公司整体名义同意了该计划。
他们合并了那家老商行。

items.meaning: the act of forming one body

items.example: The police found the corpse at dawn.
items.exampleCN: 警察在黎明发现了尸体。
温暖是身体层面的需要。

definition_en: right and free from error, or to make something right
core_image: 一支红笔把歪斜的字拉回笔直的线上
scene: 学生把答案改了三次，最后在括号里填上了对的选项。Please correct the second sentence on the board.
sceneCN: 这里 correct 指「改正」（第 2 个义项：把错误的地方改对）；句意是请改正黑板上的第二个句子。

collocations.phrase: correct me if I am wrong

senses.title: Right and without error
senses.definition: agreeing with the facts or with an accepted standard
senses.definitionCN: 与事实或公认标准相符的
senses.example: Only one of the four answers is correct.
senses.exampleCN: 四个答案里只有一个是对的。
senses.why: A straight line needs no argument about its direction.
senses.whyCN: 一条直线不必为自己的方向争辩。

senses.title: To put right
senses.definition: to change something wrong so that it becomes right
senses.definitionCN: 把错误的东西改成对的
senses.example: Please correct the second sentence on the board.
senses.exampleCN: 请改正黑板上的第二个句子。
senses.why: A small hand movement can pull a crooked line straight.
senses.whyCN: 一个小小的手势，就能把歪线拉直。

senses.title: To mark errors
senses.definition: to read work and mark the mistakes in it
senses.definitionCN: 阅读作业并标出其中的错误
senses.example: She corrects papers every evening.
senses.exampleCN: 她每天晚上批改试卷。
senses.why: A teacher's red mark is a small bridge back to the right answer.
senses.whyCN: 老师的红笔批注，是回到正确答案的一座小桥。

intro.en: Correct comes from Latin corrigere, to make straight, built from com-, together, and regere, to rule or guide straight.
intro.cn: correct 来自拉丁语 corrigere（使变直），由 com-（一起）与 regere（引导、使直）构成。

items.en: Regere meant to guide or keep something straight.
items.cn: regere 意为引导或使某物保持笔直。

items.en: Corrigere meant to straighten what had bent.
items.cn: corrigere 意为把弯掉的东西弄直。

items.en: Correctus meant made straight or set right.
items.cn: correctus 意为被弄直、被纠正的。

items.en: English correct first described a straight rule or a right form.
items.cn: 英语 correct 最初形容笔直的规则或正确的形式。

items.en: It now judges answers, manners and even wording.
items.cn: 今天它用来判断答案、举止乃至措辞是否正确。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the Latin straight base rect-, and the meaning group names other words for being right.
note.cn: 形近组共享拉丁语表示直的词基 rect-，近义组列出其他表示正确的说法。

entries.definition: to gather things together
going straight without turning
to build or set upright
true or in accordance with fact
exact and free from small errors
suitable for the situation

normalIntro.en: These hooks start with a straightened line, then move to a teacher's red pen and to a corrected answer.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从被拉直的线开始，再到老师的红笔，最后到改对的答案。

normal.en: Regere is to rule a straight line, so correct means made straight.
normal.cn: regere 是画出直线，所以 correct 就是被弄直。

normal.en: A correct answer stands up without leaning on excuses.
normal.cn: 正确答案站得直，不必靠在借口上。

normal.en: The two c letters hold the word in a straight frame.
normal.cn: 两个 c 像画框，把这个词夹在笔直的框里。

normal.en: To correct a paper is to move each wrong mark one step back.
normal.cn: 批改试卷，就是把每个错号往回挪一步。

normal.en: Correct and direct both keep the straight base rect.
normal.cn: correct 与 direct 都保留着表示直的词基 rect。

abstract.en: Picture a bent wire pulled straight by two fingers.
abstract.cn: 想象一根弯铁丝被两根手指拉直。

abstract.en: Picture a red cross turning into a neat tick.
abstract.cn: 想象一个红叉慢慢变成一个整齐的勾。

abstract.en: Picture a ruler laid along a crooked row of letters.
abstract.cn: 想象一把尺子压在一行歪斜的字母上。

examples.en: Only one of the four answers is correct.
examples.cn: 四个答案里只有一个是对的。

examples.en: The teacher corrected our spelling mistakes.
examples.cn: 老师改正了我们的拼写错误。

examples.en: He corrects papers late into the night.
examples.cn: 他批改试卷一直到深夜。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 correct 记成 cor 加 rect（直）：把弯的东西扳成直线，就是改正、使正确。

root: 源自拉丁语 corrigere（使变直、纠正），由 com-（一起）与 regere（引导、使直）构成，本指把弯的东西弄直，后引申为正确与改正。

sensesIntro.en: From a line made straight, to an error put right, and at last to the work of marking errors for others.
sensesIntro.cn: 从被弄直的线，到被改对的错误，最后到替别人标出错误的工作。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a red pen pulling a crooked stroke back to a straight line.
core.cn: 核心意象：红笔把歪斜的一笔拉回笔直的线上。

branches.en: A fact or form agrees with the standard and stands straight.
branches.cn: 事实或形式与标准相符，笔直地立着。

branches.en: A wrong thing is bent back into its right shape.
branches.cn: 错误的东西被扳回正确的形状。

branches.en: Marking is correcting done for someone else.
branches.cn: 批改就是替别人做的纠正。

branches.en: The state of being right and the act of making right share one root.
branches.cn: 正确这一状态与改对这一动作共用一个词根。

branches.en: Both move a piece of work one step toward the standard.
branches.cn: 两者都把一份作业朝标准推近一步。

intro.en: Correct is built on Latin regere, to guide straight, with the prefix com-, giving the sense of making straight.
intro.cn: correct 建立在拉丁语 regere（引导、使直）之上，加上前缀 com-，得到使变直的意思。

latinIntro.en: The straight base rect- also appears in direct, erect and rectangle.
latinIntro.cn: 表示直的词基 rect- 也出现在 direct、erect 与 rectangle 中。

items.meaning: a change that puts something right

items.example: He doubts the correctness of the claim.
items.exampleCN: 他怀疑这个说法的正确性。

definition_en: in a way that is right, exact, or suited to the situation
core_image: 一支箭正中靶心，没有偏出一指宽
scene: 实验做完后，老师提醒学生把每个数据都填在对应的格子里。If the machine is set up correctly, the light turns green.
sceneCN: 这里 correctly 指「正确地」（第 1 个义项：符合事实或规则地）；句意是如果机器设置正确，指示灯就会变绿。

senses.title: In a right way
senses.definition: in a way that follows the facts, rules or an accepted standard
senses.definitionCN: 以符合事实、规则或公认标准的方式
senses.example: She answered all six questions correctly.
senses.exampleCN: 她正确地回答了全部六个问题。
senses.why: An arrow that hits the mark needs no explanation.
senses.whyCN: 射中靶心的箭，不需要解释。

senses.title: In a proper manner
senses.definition: in a way that suits the situation or is socially acceptable
senses.definitionCN: 以适合当时情形或合乎礼貌的方式
senses.example: He behaved correctly at the formal dinner.
senses.exampleCN: 他在正式晚宴上举止得体。
senses.why: Sometimes right means fitting the room, not just the fact.
senses.whyCN: 有时正确只是说合乎这个场合，而不只是合乎事实。

intro.en: Correctly is correct plus -ly; correct goes back to Latin corrigere, to make straight, from regere, to guide straight.
intro.cn: correctly 由 correct 加 -ly 构成；correct 可追溯到拉丁语 corrigere（使变直），源自 regere（引导、使直）。

items.en: Regere meant to guide or keep straight.
items.cn: regere 意为引导或使保持笔直。

items.en: Corrigere meant to straighten what had gone crooked.
items.cn: corrigere 意为把歪掉的东西弄直。

items.en: English correct named what is straight and true.
items.cn: 英语 correct 指笔直而真实的。

items.en: The adverb correctly named the manner of getting it right.
items.cn: 副词 correctly 用来指把事情做对的方式。

items.en: It now modifies answers, settings and behaviour alike.
items.cn: 今天它同样修饰答案、设置与举止。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the straight base rect-, and the meaning group names other adverbs of being right.
note.cn: 形近组共享表示直的词基 rect-，近义组列出其他表示正确地、恰当地的说法。

entries.definition: right and free from error
a change that puts something right
meant to put something right
for a good or true reason
in a suitable or correct way
with exactness and care

normalIntro.en: These hooks start with an arrow in the centre, then move to a machine set right and to polite behaviour.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从正中靶心的箭开始，再到设置正确的机器，最后到得体的举止。

normal.en: Correct is the straight answer, and -ly turns it into the way of doing it.
normal.cn: correct 是笔直的答案，加 -ly 就变成做这件事的方式。

normal.en: If the light turns green, the machine was set correctly.
normal.cn: 如果灯变绿，说明机器设对了。

normal.en: Correctly is the adverb you hear beside verbs like answer and spell.
normal.cn: correctly 常跟在 answer 和 spell 这类动词旁边。

normal.en: One extra finger of error and the word would be wrongly.
normal.cn: 偏出一指，这个词就变成 wrongly 了。

normal.en: Remember the double r in the middle: cor-rect-ly.
normal.cn: 记住中间有两个 r：cor-rect-ly。

abstract.en: Picture an arrow trembling, then settling in the gold.
abstract.cn: 想象一支箭抖了一下，最后停在靶心。

abstract.en: Picture two lines laid exactly on top of each other.
abstract.cn: 想象两条线严丝合缝地叠在一起。

abstract.en: Picture a key sliding in without a single scrape.
abstract.cn: 想象一把钥匙毫无摩擦地滑进锁孔。

examples.en: She answered all six questions correctly.
examples.cn: 她正确地回答了全部六个问题。

examples.en: The clock has not worked correctly since Monday.
examples.cn: 从周一起这只钟就走得不准。

examples.en: If I remember correctly, the shop closes at six.
examples.cn: 如果我没记错，这家店六点关门。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 correctly 记成 correct（正确的）加 ly：以正确的方式做，就是正确地。

root: 由 correct 加副词词尾 -ly 构成；correct 源自拉丁语 corrigere（使变直），词基 regere 意为引导、使直。

sensesIntro.en: From hitting the exact mark, to behaving in a way that fits the room.
sensesIntro.cn: 从正中靶心，到举止合乎场合。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an arrow settling exactly in the gold.
core.cn: 核心意象：一支箭稳稳落在靶心。

branches.en: The answer matches the fact, so no mark is lost.
branches.cn: 答案与事实相符，所以一分不失。

branches.en: The behaviour matches the room, so no one is embarrassed.
branches.cn: 举止与场合相符，所以没人尴尬。

branches.en: Both uses say that a standard has been met.
branches.cn: 两种用法都表示达到了某个标准。

branches.en: Polite correctness often matters more than bare truth.
branches.cn: 礼貌上的得体，往往比赤裸的真相更要紧。

branches.en: Careful checking is how correctness is proved.
branches.cn: 仔细核对，是证明正确的方式。

intro.en: Correctly is correct plus the adverb ending -ly, resting on Latin regere, to guide straight.
intro.cn: correctly 由 correct 加副词词尾 -ly 构成，根源是拉丁语 regere（引导、使直）。

latinIntro.en: The straight base rect- also shapes rectify, direct and erect.
latinIntro.cn: 表示直的词基 rect- 也构成 rectify、direct 与 erect。

items.example: They checked the correctness of the data.
items.exampleCN: 他们核对了数据的正确性。

items.example: The form was filled in incorrectly.

definition_en: to match or agree with something, to exchange letters, or to be equivalent to something
core_image: 两封信在邮路上相对而行，信里的字句一模一样
scene: 两张地图摊在桌上，河的弯道一处接一处地对上了。The two maps correspond at every bend of the river.
sceneCN: 这里 correspond 指「相符」（第 1 个义项：彼此一致）；句意是两张地图在河的每个弯道处都吻合。

senses.title: To match
senses.definition: to be similar to or in agreement with something else
senses.definitionCN: 与另一事物相似或一致
senses.example: His account corresponds with the facts.
senses.exampleCN: 他的说法与事实相符。
senses.why: Two shapes laid over each other show at once whether they fit.
senses.whyCN: 两个形状叠在一起，立刻就能看出是否吻合。

senses.title: To exchange letters
senses.definition: to write letters to someone and receive letters from them
senses.definitionCN: 给某人写信并收到对方的来信
senses.example: They corresponded for ten years before they met.
senses.exampleCN: 他们通信十年后才见面。
senses.why: A letter is an answer that travels a long way to arrive.
senses.whyCN: 一封信就是一个走了很远路才到达的回答。

senses.title: To be equivalent
senses.definition: to be the same as or to represent something else
senses.definitionCN: 等同于或代表另一事物
senses.example: This word corresponds to a short phrase in English.
senses.exampleCN: 这个词相当于英语里的一个短语。
senses.why: Two languages keep separate rooms for the same meaning.
senses.whyCN: 两种语言为同一个意思各留了一间房。

intro.en: Correspond joins Latin com-, together, and respondere, to answer, so it first meant to answer in turn.
intro.cn: correspond 由拉丁语 com-（一起）与 respondere（回答）组合，本指轮流作答。

items.en: Respondere meant to answer or promise back.
items.cn: respondere 意为回答或回以承诺。

items.en: Correspondere meant to answer one another.
items.cn: correspondere 意为彼此应答。

items.en: Old French correspondre kept the sense of answering in turn.
items.cn: 古法语 correspondre 保留了轮流应答的意思。

items.en: English correspond added the sense of fitting or matching.
items.cn: 英语 correspond 增加了吻合、相符的意思。

items.en: It now covers matching facts, swapping letters and equal values.
items.cn: 今天它涵盖事实相符、书信往来与数值相当。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the answering base respond-, and the meaning group names other words for matching and writing.
note.cn: 形近组共享表示回答的词基 respond-，近义组列出其他表示吻合与通信的说法。

entries.definition: letters exchanged between people
a reporter based in a place
matching or related in position
to be the same as or go well with
to have the same opinion or to be consistent
to treat two things as equal

normalIntro.en: These hooks start with two shapes that fit, then move to letters crossing in the post and to equal values.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从两个吻合的形状开始，再到邮路上交错的书信，最后到相等的数值。

normal.en: Respond means answer, so correspond means answer back and forth.
normal.cn: respond 是回答，correspond 就是你来我往地回应。

normal.en: Two maps that agree bend for bend correspond.
normal.cn: 两张弯道处处一致的地图，就是 correspond。

normal.en: The co- at the front means the answer goes both ways.
normal.cn: 开头的 co- 表示回答是双向的。

normal.en: When facts answer each other, they correspond.
normal.cn: 当事实彼此呼应时，它们就是相符的。

normal.en: Writing letters is just corresponding with a slow voice.
normal.cn: 写信不过是用一个缓慢的声音通信。

abstract.en: Picture two keys turning in locks at the same moment.
abstract.cn: 想象两把钥匙在同一刻转动锁孔。

abstract.en: Picture two envelopes crossing above a dark sea.
abstract.cn: 想象两个信封在漆黑的海面上交错而过。

abstract.en: Picture one meaning standing in two different rooms.
abstract.cn: 想象同一个意思站在两间不同的屋子里。

examples.en: His account corresponds with the facts.
examples.cn: 他的说法与事实相符。

examples.en: They corresponded for ten years before they met.
examples.cn: 他们通信十年后才见面。

examples.en: This symbol corresponds to the sound of s.
examples.cn: 这个符号相当于 s 的读音。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 correspond 记成 co（共同）加 respond（回答）：彼此互相回答，就是相符、通信。

root: 源自拉丁语 correspondere，由 com-（一起）与 respondere（回答）构成，本指彼此应答，后引申为相符、通信与相当。

sensesIntro.en: From answering one another, to facts fitting together, to letters crossing and to values that balance.
sensesIntro.cn: 从彼此应答，到事实相互吻合，再到书信交错与数值相当。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two letters meeting halfway, their lines identical.
core.cn: 核心意象：两封信在半路相遇，字句一模一样。

branches.en: Two accounts answer each other and agree.
branches.cn: 两种说法彼此呼应，取得一致。

branches.en: Two people keep answering by post.
branches.cn: 两个人靠书信不断回应对方。

branches.en: Two systems hold the same value in different forms.
branches.cn: 两套体系以不同形式装着同一个值。

branches.en: Matching and equating both rest on one-to-one alignment.
branches.cn: 吻合与相当都建立在逐一对应之上。

branches.en: A letter and a symbol can both stand for something absent.
branches.cn: 一封信与一个符号，都能代表不在场的事物。

intro.en: Correspond is Latin com-, together, plus respondere, to answer, giving the sense of answering in turn.
intro.cn: correspond 由拉丁语 com-（一起）与 respondere（回答）组成，意为轮流应答。

latinIntro.en: The answering base spons- also appears in response, responsible and sponsor.
latinIntro.cn: 表示回答与承诺的词基 spons- 也出现在 response、responsible 与 sponsor 中。

pos.zh: 通信；信件往来；一致；对应

senses.title: Letters going both ways
senses.definition: the writing and receiving of letters between people
senses.definitionCN: 人与人之间写信与收信的活动
senses.example: Their correspondence lasted more than twenty years.
senses.exampleCN: 他们的通信持续了二十多年。
senses.why: Two pens answer each other across a long silence.
senses.whyCN: 两支笔隔着漫长的沉默互相回答。

senses.title: A close agreement
senses.definition: a strong similarity between two accounts or sets of facts
senses.definitionCN: 两种说法或两组事实之间的高度相似
senses.example: There is a close correspondence between the two reports.
senses.exampleCN: 这两份报告高度一致。
senses.why: Two maps of one valley should agree on every bend.
senses.whyCN: 同一山谷的两张地图，应该在每个弯道处一致。

senses.title: A one-to-one link
senses.definition: a direct relationship in which each item on one side matches an item on the other
senses.definitionCN: 一方每一项都与另一方某一项相匹配的直接关系
senses.example: The chart shows the correspondence between sounds and symbols.
senses.exampleCN: 这张表显示了声音与符号之间的对应关系。
senses.why: Every key needs its own lock, and every sign its own meaning.
senses.whyCN: 每把钥匙都要有自己的锁，每个符号都要有自己的意思。

intro.en: Correspondence comes from Latin correspondere, to answer one another, from com-, together, and respondere, to answer.

items.en: Respondere meant to answer or give a promise back.

items.en: Correspondere meant to answer each other in turn.

items.en: Old French kept the word for an exchange of answers.
items.cn: 古法语保留了这个词，指回答的往来。

items.en: English correspondence named the exchange of letters.

items.en: It also names any tight fit between two sets of things.
items.cn: 它也表示两组事物之间严密的吻合。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the answering base respond-, and the meaning group names other words for letters and agreement.
note.cn: 形近组共享表示回答的词基 respond-，近义组列出其他表示书信与一致的说法。

entries.definition: to match or exchange letters

matching in position or meaning

normal.en: A correspondence can be a box of letters or a perfect fit.

normal.cn: 结尾 -ence 与 difference 里的那个一样。

normal.en: A correspondence course travels by post instead of by bus.
normal.cn: 函授课程靠邮路而不是靠公交车来上课。

abstract.en: Picture two pens dipping into one inkwell, years apart.
abstract.cn: 想象两支笔隔着多年，蘸进同一只墨水瓶。

abstract.en: Picture two maps with every river drawn in the same place.
abstract.cn: 想象两张地图把每条河都画在同一个位置。

abstract.en: Picture a row of keys facing a row of locks.
abstract.cn: 想象一排钥匙正对着一排锁。

examples.en: Their correspondence lasted more than twenty years.
examples.cn: 他们的通信持续了二十多年。

examples.en: There is a close correspondence between the two reports.
examples.cn: 这两份报告高度一致。

examples.en: She keeps her business correspondence in a grey box.
examples.cn: 她把商业信函放在一只灰色的盒子里。

root: 源自拉丁语 correspondere（彼此应答），由 com-（一起）与 respondere（回答）构成，本指互相回应，后指书信往来与彼此一致。

sensesIntro.en: From letters answering each other, to reports that agree, and at last to signs paired with meanings.
sensesIntro.cn: 从彼此回应的书信，到互相一致的报告，最后到符号与意义的成对关系。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a wooden box packed with letters that travelled both ways.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只木盒塞满来回旅行过的信。

branches.en: Two writers keep answering across the distance.
branches.cn: 两位写信人隔着距离不断回应。

branches.en: Two accounts of one event fit without a gap.
branches.cn: 同一事件的两种说法严丝合缝。

branches.en: Each sign on one side faces one sign on the other.
branches.cn: 一边的每个符号都对着另一边的某个符号。

branches.en: Letters and reports both aim at a meeting of two sides.
branches.cn: 书信与报告都指向两方的会合。

branches.en: Agreement in meaning and pairing in form are cousins.
branches.cn: 意思上的一致与形式上的配对是近亲。

intro.en: Correspondence is correspond plus the noun ending -ence, from Latin respondere, to answer.
intro.cn: correspondence 由 correspond 加名词词尾 -ence 构成，源于拉丁语 respondere（回答）。

latinIntro.en: The answering base spons- also runs through response, responsible and sponsor.
latinIntro.cn: 表示回答与承诺的词基 spons- 也贯穿 response、responsible 与 sponsor。

items.meaning: an exchange of answers or letters

items.example: He is responsible for the file.

definition_zh: 记者；通讯员；通信者；对应物
definition_en: a reporter based in a particular place, or a person who writes letters
core_image: 一个人蹲在战壕边，对着电话把远处的火光说给编辑部
scene: 战地记者蹲在掩体后，用卫星电话向编辑部口述现场。The correspondent sent her report from the border.
sceneCN: 这里 correspondent 指「派驻记者」（第 1 个义项：被派往某地报道的人）；句意是这位记者从边境发回了报道。

pos.zh: 记者；通讯员；通信者；对应物

senses.title: A reporter in the field
senses.definition: a journalist who reports from a particular place or on a particular subject
senses.definitionCN: 从某地或就某专题发回报道的新闻工作者
senses.example: The correspondent sent her report from the border.
senses.exampleCN: 这位记者从边境发回了报道。
senses.why: News needs a pair of eyes that live where the story lives.
senses.whyCN: 新闻需要一双住在其发生地的眼睛。

senses.title: A person who writes letters
senses.definition: someone who exchanges letters with another person
senses.definitionCN: 与另一个人互相写信的人
senses.example: She has been a faithful correspondent for years.
senses.exampleCN: 多年来她一直是个忠实的通信者。
senses.why: A letter is a visit that waits quietly in the post box.
senses.whyCN: 一封信就是一次拜访，静静等在信箱里。

senses.title: A matching counterpart
senses.definition: a thing that matches or corresponds to another
senses.definitionCN: 与另一事物相匹配或相对应的事物
senses.example: This verb is the correspondent of that noun.
senses.exampleCN: 这个动词是那个名词的对应形式。
senses.why: Two forms of one meaning stand facing each other.
senses.whyCN: 同一个意思的两种形式，面对面站着。

intro.en: Correspondent is the person noun from correspond, built on Latin correspondere, to answer one another.
intro.cn: correspondent 是 correspond 的人物名词，源自拉丁语 correspondere（彼此应答）。

items.en: Respondere meant to answer or promise back.
items.cn: respondere 意为回答或回以承诺。

items.en: Correspondere meant to answer one another.
items.cn: correspondere 意为彼此应答。

items.en: The noun named someone who answers or writes.
items.cn: 这个名词指作答或写信的人。

items.en: English correspondent came to mean a writer of news from far away.
items.cn: 英语 correspondent 逐渐指从远方写回新闻的人。

items.en: It now names both reporters and steady letter writers.
items.cn: 今天它既指记者，也指长期通信的人。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the answering base respond-, and the meaning group names other people who report or write.
note.cn: 形近组共享表示回答的词基 respond-，近义组列出其他报道或写信的人。

entries.definition: to match or exchange letters
letters exchanged or a close match
related one to one
a person who gathers and reports news
a person who writes for newspapers or magazines
entries.definitionCN: 为报纸或杂志写作的人

entries.definition: a friend known only through letters
entries.definitionCN: 只通过书信交往的朋友

normalIntro.en: These hooks start with a voice calling from a distant border, then move to a steady letter writer and to a matching form.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从远方边境传来的声音开始，再到忠实的写信人，最后到相对应的形式。

normal.en: A correspondent answers the world with a report.
normal.cn: 记者用一篇报道回应整个世界。

normal.en: The word ends in -ent, like agent and student, so it names a person.
normal.cn: 这个词以 -ent 结尾，像 agent 和 student，因此指人。

normal.en: A war correspondent carries a notebook where others carry a gun.
normal.cn: 战地记者带着笔记本，别人带着枪。

normal.en: A pen friend is a correspondent who never knocks at the door.
normal.cn: 笔友是一位从不上门敲门的通信者。

normal.en: If two forms match, each is the correspondent of the other.
normal.cn: 如果两种形式相配，彼此就是对方的对应物。

abstract.en: Picture a microphone held out toward a distant fire.
abstract.cn: 想象一支话筒伸向远处的火光。

abstract.en: Picture a letter arriving every winter without fail.
abstract.cn: 想象每年冬天都准时到达的一封信。

abstract.en: Picture two words standing face to face like mirrors.
abstract.cn: 想象两个词像镜子一样面对面站着。

examples.en: The correspondent sent her report from the border.
examples.cn: 这位记者从边境发回了报道。

examples.en: She has been a faithful correspondent for years.
examples.cn: 多年来她一直是个忠实的通信者。

examples.en: A foreign correspondent often works alone.
examples.cn: 驻外记者常常独自工作。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 correspondent 记成 correspond（互相回应）加 ent（人）：替远方回应世界的人，就是记者与通信者。

root: 源自拉丁语 correspondere（彼此应答），由 com-（一起）与 respondere（回答）构成，加上人物词尾 -ent，指回应与报道的人。

sensesIntro.en: From a reporter answering the world, to a letter writer answering a friend, and at last to a form answering another form.
sensesIntro.cn: 从回应世界的记者，到回应朋友的写信人，最后到回应另一种形式的形式。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a voice at a distant border speaking into a telephone.
core.cn: 核心意象：远方边境的一个声音对着电话说话。

branches.en: The reporter stands where the news is happening.
branches.cn: 记者站在新闻正在发生的地方。

branches.en: The letter writer keeps a quiet conversation alive.
branches.cn: 写信人让一场安静的对话持续下去。

branches.en: A matching form answers another form one to one.
branches.cn: 对应的形式与另一形式逐一呼应。

branches.en: Both answer someone far away, one by news and one by letter.
branches.cn: 两者都在回应远方的人，一个用新闻，一个用书信。

branches.en: A steady writer and a matching form both keep a link unbroken.
branches.cn: 忠实的写信人与对应的形式，都让一条联系不断。

intro.en: Correspondent is correspond plus -ent, a person ending, from Latin respondere, to answer.
intro.cn: correspondent 由 correspond 加人物词尾 -ent 构成，源于拉丁语 respondere（回答）。

latinIntro.en: The answering base spons- also appears in response, responsible and sponsor.
latinIntro.cn: 表示回答与承诺的词基 spons- 也出现在 response、responsible 与 sponsor 中。

definition_en: a long narrow passage inside a building, or a narrow strip of land between two areas
core_image: 一条长长的通道，两侧的门一扇接一扇，尽头透进白光
scene: 医院三楼的走廊很长，尽头那扇窗透进一片白光。A nurse walked quickly down the corridor.
sceneCN: 这里 corridor 指「走廊」（第 1 个义项：建筑物内连接房间的长通道）；句意是一位护士快步走过走廊。

collocations.phrase: at the end of the corridor

derivatives.zh: 信使；快递员（与 corridor 同源于「跑」）
光标（同源词，本指奔跑者）

senses.title: A passage inside a building
senses.definition: a long narrow passage that connects rooms in a building
senses.definitionCN: 建筑物内连接各个房间的狭长通道
senses.example: A nurse walked quickly down the corridor.
senses.exampleCN: 一位护士快步走过走廊。
senses.why: A building needs a spine so that its rooms can be one body.
senses.whyCN: 建筑需要一根脊梁，房间才能连成一个身体。

senses.title: A strip of land
senses.definition: a narrow piece of land that joins two larger areas
senses.definitionCN: 连接两片较大区域的狭长土地
senses.example: The road runs through a narrow corridor of land.
senses.exampleCN: 这条路穿过一条狭长地带。
senses.why: Countries also need passages, and they guard them like doors.
senses.whyCN: 国家也需要通道，并像守门一样守着它们。

senses.title: The aisle of a train
senses.definition: the narrow walking space between seats in a train or plane
senses.definitionCN: 火车或飞机座位之间供人行走的窄道
senses.example: He stood in the corridor with his ticket.
senses.exampleCN: 他拿着车票站在车厢过道里。
senses.why: Even a moving box needs a line along which people pass.
senses.whyCN: 即使是一只移动的盒子，也需要一条让人通过的线。

intro.en: Corridor comes from Italian corridore, a runner or running place, from correre, to run, and Latin currere.
intro.cn: corridor 来自意大利语 corridore（奔跑者、跑道），源自 correre（跑）与拉丁语 currere。

items.en: Currere meant to run.
items.cn: currere 意为奔跑。

items.en: Corridore named a runner or a place for running.
items.cn: corridore 指奔跑的人或供奔跑的地方。

items.en: French corridor named a narrow passage in a fortress.
items.cn: 法语 corridor 指堡垒中的狭窄通道。

items.en: English corridor first meant a covered walk or gallery.
items.cn: 英语 corridor 最初指有顶的步道或长廊。

items.en: It now means any long passage, in a building or on a map.
items.cn: 今天它指任何长通道，无论在大楼里还是地图上。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the running base curr-, and the meaning group names other ways through a building.
note.cn: 形近组共享表示奔跑的词基 curr-，近义组列出其他穿过建筑的说法。

entries.definition: to eat away metal slowly
to drive animals into an enclosure
a ring of light around the sun
a passage just inside the front door
a narrow way from one place to another
entries.definitionCN: 从一处通向另一处的窄道

entries.definition: the space between rows of seats

normalIntro.en: These hooks start with a long passage lined with doors, then move to a narrow strip of land and to a train aisle.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从两侧都是门的长通道开始，再到狭长地带，最后到车厢过道。

normal.en: Corridor comes from a word for running, so it is a place made for moving.
normal.cn: corridor 源自表示奔跑的词，所以它是为移动而设的地方。

normal.en: A corridor has two rows of doors and no chairs.
normal.cn: 走廊有两排门，却没有椅子。

normal.en: Hospitals keep corridors long so that beds can pass.
normal.cn: 医院把走廊修得长，是为了让病床通过。

normal.en: A land corridor is a hallway between two countries.
normal.cn: 陆上走廊就是两国之间的一条过道。

normal.en: The double r in the middle keeps the word running.
normal.cn: 中间的两个 r 让这个词一直向前跑。

abstract.en: Picture a line of doors standing one behind another.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇扇门一层层排在身后。

abstract.en: Picture a thin neck of land joining two wide rooms.
abstract.cn: 想象一条细长的陆地，把两片宽阔的土地连起来。

abstract.en: Picture light at the far end of a very long tunnel.
abstract.cn: 想象一条很长隧道的尽头有光。

examples.en: A nurse walked quickly down the corridor.
examples.cn: 一位护士快步走过走廊。

examples.en: Their office is at the end of the corridor.
examples.cn: 他们的办公室在走廊尽头。

examples.en: The train corridor was full of luggage.
examples.cn: 火车过道里堆满了行李。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 corridor 记成「能跑的道」：两侧是门、中间能一路跑到尽头，就是走廊。

root: 源自意大利语 corridore（奔跑者、跑道），来自 correre（跑），再上溯到拉丁语 currere（奔跑），本指供人穿行的长道。

sensesIntro.en: From a passage between rooms, to a thin strip of land, and at last to the aisle of a moving carriage.
sensesIntro.cn: 从房间之间的通道，到一条细长的土地，最后到移动车厢里的过道。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a long narrow passage with doors on both sides.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条长而窄的通道，两侧都是门。

branches.en: The corridor turns separate rooms into one building.
branches.cn: 走廊把一个个房间变成一栋完整的建筑。

branches.en: A narrow strip of land turns two areas into neighbours.
branches.cn: 一条狭长土地把两片区域变成邻居。

branches.en: An aisle lets people pass while the carriage moves.
branches.cn: 过道让人们在车厢移动时仍能通行。

branches.en: Both are thin lines that join larger spaces.
branches.cn: 两者都是连接较大空间的细线。

branches.en: Land corridor and train aisle are both narrow routes of passage.
branches.cn: 陆上走廊与车厢过道都是狭窄的通行路线。

intro.en: Corridor is built on Latin currere, to run, through Italian corridore, a running place.
intro.cn: corridor 建立在拉丁语 currere（奔跑）之上，经意大利语 corridore（跑道）而来。

latinIntro.en: The running base curr- also appears in current, cursor and excursion.
latinIntro.cn: 表示奔跑的词基 curr- 也出现在 current、cursor 与 excursion 中。

items.meaning: a train with a side passage
items.example: The corridor train stops at every town.
items.exampleCN: 这趟走廊式列车逢站就停。

items.meaning: a carriage with a side passage
items.example: We sat in the corridor coach.
items.exampleCN: 我们坐在走廊式车厢里。

items.meaning: a path or direction of movement
water or air that runs forward
a moving mark on a screen

definition_en: the money needed to buy or make something, the loss suffered for a gain, or to have a price
core_image: 一张价签挂在货物上，背后还压着一本看不见的账
scene: 装修报价单摊在桌上，木地板那一项比预期高出一截。The repairs will cost more than we planned.
sceneCN: 这里 cost 指「花费」（第 3 个义项：需要付出某笔钱）；句意是这次维修的花费会超出我们的计划。

senses.title: The money needed
senses.definition: the amount of money that must be paid to buy or make something
senses.definitionCN: 为购买或制造某物必须支付的金额
senses.example: The cost of the ticket surprised us.
senses.exampleCN: 票价让我们吃了一惊。
senses.why: Every object carries an invisible price tag on its back.
senses.whyCN: 每件物品背后都挂着一张看不见的价签。

senses.title: What a gain takes from you
senses.definition: the loss or damage suffered in order to gain something
senses.definitionCN: 为获得某物而承受的损失或损害
senses.example: He won the match at the cost of his health.
senses.exampleCN: 他赢了比赛，代价是健康。
senses.why: Every victory is paid for with something that is not money.
senses.whyCN: 每一场胜利都要用钱以外的东西来支付。

senses.title: To have a price
senses.definition: to have a particular price, or to make someone lose something
senses.definitionCN: 价格为某数，或使某人失去某物
senses.example: The repairs will cost more than we planned.
senses.exampleCN: 这次维修的花费会超出我们的计划。
senses.why: The price reaches out from the object and takes money from your hand.
senses.whyCN: 价格从物品那边伸出手，把你手中的钱拿走。

intro.en: Cost comes from Latin constare, to stand firm or stand at a price, through Old French coster, to cost.
intro.cn: cost 来自拉丁语 constare（立定、值某个价钱），经古法语 coster（值…钱）进入英语。

items.en: Constare meant to stand together or stand firm.
items.cn: constare 意为共同站立或稳稳立住。

items.en: The same verb came to mean to stand at a certain price.
items.cn: 同一个动词后来表示标价为某个数目。

items.en: Coster meant to cost or be bought for a sum.
items.cn: coster 意为值多少钱、以某价购得。

items.en: English cost named the price paid for a thing.
items.cn: 英语 cost 指为某物付出的价钱。

items.en: It also names the price paid in effort, time or health.
items.cn: 它也指用精力、时间或健康付出的代价。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers short words in -ost or -ast, and the meaning group names other words for what is paid.
note.cn: 形近组收集以 -ost 或 -ast 结尾的短词，近义组列出其他表示所付之物的说法。

entries.definition: the land beside the sea
to throw something with force
a piece of outer clothing
the money asked for a thing
money spent on a purpose
the money demanded for a service

normalIntro.en: These hooks start with a price tag, then move to a victory paid for in health and to a repair that empties a wallet.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从一张价签开始，再到用健康换来的胜利，最后到掏空钱包的维修。

normal.en: Cost is the price tag plus everything the price tag hides.
normal.cn: cost 是价签，也是价签藏起来的一切。

normal.en: The past tense does not change: it cost, it has cost.
normal.cn: 过去式不变：it cost，it has cost。

normal.en: Cheap things often cost more in the end.
normal.cn: 便宜的东西，最后往往花费更多。

normal.en: A costly mistake is one whose price arrives later.
normal.cn: 代价惨重的错误，就是账单迟到的错误。

normal.en: Effort, time and sleep can all be costs.
normal.cn: 精力、时间和睡眠都可以是代价。

abstract.en: Picture a coin lying on one pan of a balance.
abstract.cn: 想象一枚硬币躺在天平的一端。

abstract.en: Picture a receipt longer than the thing you bought.
abstract.cn: 想象一张比你买的东西还长的收据。

abstract.en: Picture a door marked free with a small lock on it.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇写着免费的门，上面挂着一把小锁。

examples.en: The repairs will cost more than we planned.
examples.cn: 这次维修的花费会超出我们的计划。

examples.en: The ticket costs a week of his wages.
examples.cn: 这张票要花掉他一周的工资。

examples.en: He won the match at the cost of his health.
examples.cn: 他赢了比赛，代价是健康。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 cost 记成「扣死他」：价格一扣，钱就没了，所以是花费与代价。

root: 源自拉丁语 constare（共同立定、值某个价钱），经古法语 coster 进入英语，本指物品所值之价，后引申为一切代价。

sensesIntro.en: From money on a tag, to a loss that is not money, and at last to the act of taking money from a pocket.
sensesIntro.cn: 从价签上的钱，到不是钱的损失，最后到从口袋里拿走钱这一动作。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a price tag with a hidden ledger behind it.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张价签，背后压着一本看不见的账。

branches.en: A sum of money is named before the deal.
branches.cn: 交易之前先说出一个钱数。

branches.en: Something other than money is taken away.
branches.cn: 被拿走的不是钱，而是别的东西。

branches.en: The verb makes the object reach into your pocket.
branches.cn: 动词使物品伸手进你的口袋。

branches.en: The noun and the verb name the same money from two sides.
branches.cn: 名词与动词从两侧说同一笔钱。

branches.en: To cost can mean to take away health, time or peace.
branches.cn: 花费也可以指拿走健康、时间或安宁。

intro.en: Cost is a short base word from Latin constare, to stand at a price, with many modern compounds.
intro.cn: cost 是来自拉丁语 constare（标价）的短词根词，现代又生出许多复合词。

latinIntro.en: The standing base sta- also appears in constant, stable and stand.
latinIntro.cn: 表示站立的词基 sta- 也出现在 constant、stable 与 stand 中。

items.meaning: giving good value for the money
the price paid by the seller

items.exampleCN: 削减开支救了这家公司。

definition_en: costing a lot of money, or causing serious loss or damage
core_image: 一只钱包被打开，里面只剩几枚硬币和一张长账单
scene: 球队赢了决赛，却伤了两名主力，教练说这场胜利太贵了。Winning the cup proved costly for the small club.
sceneCN: 这里 costly 指「代价惨重的」（第 2 个义项：带来严重损失）；句意是赢得奖杯对这家小俱乐部来说代价惨重。

senses.title: Very expensive
senses.definition: costing a great deal of money
senses.definitionCN: 需要花费大量金钱的
senses.example: The repairs were costly but necessary.
senses.exampleCN: 这次维修很贵，却非做不可。
senses.why: A high price tag makes the hand stop before the pocket.
senses.whyCN: 高价签让手在伸向口袋之前停住。

senses.title: Paid for in loss
senses.definition: causing serious loss, damage or suffering
senses.definitionCN: 造成严重损失、损害或痛苦的
senses.example: Winning the cup proved costly for the small club.

senses.why: Some bills arrive without money and are still paid in full.

intro.en: Costly is cost plus the old adjective ending -ly, from Latin constare, to stand at a price.
intro.cn: costly 由 cost 加古形容词词尾 -ly 构成，根源是拉丁语 constare（标价）。

items.en: Constare meant to stand at a price.
items.cn: constare 意为标价为某个数目。

items.en: Coster meant to cost or be bought for a sum.
items.cn: coster 意为值多少钱、以某价购得。

items.en: English cost named the price of a thing.
items.cn: 英语 cost 指某物的价钱。

items.en: The ending -ly turned it into an adjective of high price.
items.cn: 词尾 -ly 把它变成表示高价的形容词。

items.en: It now describes both heavy bills and heavy losses.
items.cn: 今天它既形容高额账单，也形容沉重损失。

note.en: The look-alike group keeps the cost family together, and the meaning group names other words for a high price.
note.cn: 形近组把 cost 家族放在一起，近义组列出其他表示昂贵的说法。

entries.definition: the price paid for something
the work of calculating costs
free of charge
costing a lot of money
high in price in British use

entries.definition: rather expensive in an informal way

normalIntro.en: These hooks start with a thin purse, then move to a victory that hurt and to a repair bill that grows.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从一只瘪钱包开始，再到一场伤人的胜利，最后到不断上涨的维修账单。

normal.en: Cost plus -ly means full of cost, the way friendly means full of friend.
normal.cn: cost 加 -ly 表示满是花费，就像 friendly 表示满是人情。

normal.en: A costly mistake sends its bill months later.
normal.cn: 代价惨重的错误，几个月后才寄来账单。

normal.en: The comparative is costlier, not more costly.
normal.cn: 比较级是 costlier，不是 more costly。

normal.en: A costly victory is a win that feels like a loss.
normal.cn: 惨胜就是一场感觉像失败的胜利。

normal.en: Cheap now, costly later: the same word fits both.
normal.cn: 现在便宜，以后昂贵，同一个词都能形容。

abstract.en: Picture a receipt that grows longer as it falls.
abstract.cn: 想象一张收据往下掉时越变越长。

abstract.en: Picture a trophy with a crack running through it.
abstract.cn: 想象一座奖杯上有一道裂纹穿过。

abstract.en: Picture a purse with one coin and one shadow.
abstract.cn: 想象一只钱包里只有一枚硬币和一道影子。

examples.en: Winning the cup proved costly for the small club.
examples.cn: 赢得奖杯对这家小俱乐部来说代价惨重。

examples.en: The repairs were costly but necessary.
examples.cn: 这次维修很贵，却非做不可。

examples.en: A moment of anger can be the costliest mistake.
examples.cn: 一时的怒气可能成为代价最大的错误。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 costly 记成 cost（花费）加 ly：处处要花钱，就是昂贵的、代价大的。

root: 由 cost（花费、代价）加形容词词尾 -ly 构成；cost 源自拉丁语 constare（标价），经古法语 coster 而来。

sensesIntro.en: From a high price on a tag, to a loss that never appears on any tag.
sensesIntro.cn: 从价签上的高价，到永远不出现在价签上的损失。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a wallet opened to show one coin and a long bill.
core.cn: 核心意象：钱包打开，只剩一枚硬币和一张长账单。

branches.en: Money leaves the pocket quickly and visibly.
branches.cn: 钱从口袋离开，又快又看得见。

branches.en: Something precious is lost and the bill is invisible.
branches.cn: 珍贵的东西失去了，账单却看不见。

branches.en: Both uses measure what a thing takes from you.
branches.cn: 两种用法都在衡量一件事从你身上拿走了什么。

branches.en: A costly win can cost health, trust or time.
branches.cn: 代价惨重的胜利，可能搭上健康、信任或时间。

branches.en: The adjective often leans on the word mistake.
branches.cn: 这个形容词常与 mistake 这个词搭配。

intro.en: Costly is a base word plus -ly, an old adjective ending that means having the quality of.
intro.cn: costly 是词根词加 -ly 构成，这个古老形容词词尾表示具有某种性质。

latinIntro.en: The standing base sta- also appears in constant, stable and station.
latinIntro.cn: 表示站立的词基 sta- 也出现在 constant、stable 与 station 中。

items.meaning: price or to have a price

definition_en: a small house, especially in the countryside, or a small house used for holidays
core_image: 一栋石头小屋，茅草屋顶上飘着一缕细烟
scene: 雨落在茅草顶上，烟囱冒出细细一缕烟。They spent the summer in a small cottage by the sea.
sceneCN: 这里 cottage 指「乡村小屋」（第 1 个义项：乡下的小房子）；句意是他们在海边的一间小屋度过了夏天。

senses.title: A small country house
senses.definition: a small simple house, especially in the countryside
senses.definitionCN: 尤指乡下的简朴小房子
senses.example: They spent the summer in a small cottage by the sea.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在海边的一间小屋度过了夏天。
senses.why: Small walls and a low roof keep a country life warm.
senses.whyCN: 矮墙低顶，把乡间的生活捂得暖暖的。

senses.title: A house for holidays
senses.definition: a small house that people rent or keep for short holidays
senses.definitionCN: 人们租用或留着短期度假的小房子
senses.example: We rented a cottage in the hills for a week.
senses.exampleCN: 我们在山里租了一间小屋住了一周。
senses.why: A holiday needs a roof smaller than the life you left behind.
senses.whyCN: 度假需要一个比原先生活更小的屋顶。

intro.en: Cottage goes back to Old English cot, a small hut, with the French ending -age added in medieval times.
intro.cn: cottage 可追溯到古英语 cot（小屋），中世纪时加上法语词尾 -age。

items.en: Cot meant a small hut or shelter.
items.cn: cot 意为小茅屋或遮蔽处。

items.en: Cotagium named a small dwelling with a little land.
items.cn: cotagium 指带一小块土地的小住所。

items.en: Cottage named the house of a country worker.
items.cn: cottage 指乡间劳动者的住房。

items.en: English cottage meant a small rural house.
items.cn: 英语 cottage 指乡间的小房子。

items.en: It now also names small houses kept for holidays.
items.cn: 今天它也指留着度假用的小屋。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers short words near the shape of cottage, and the meaning group names other small dwellings.
note.cn: 形近组收集形状接近 cottage 的短词，近义组列出其他小型住所。

entries.definition: a place of higher or further education
entries.definitionCN: 高等教育或继续教育的场所

entries.definition: a poor farm worker with a small cottage
entries.definitionCN: 只有一间小屋的贫苦农业雇工

entries.definition: a small shelter for birds or animals
a small simple wooden house
a very small and simple shelter
a small house used for hunting or holidays

normalIntro.en: These hooks start with a stone wall and a low roof, then move to a rented holiday house in the hills.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从石头墙和低屋顶开始，再到山里租来的度假小屋。

normal.en: Cot is an old word for a small hut, and -age makes it a place.
normal.cn: cot 是表示小茅屋的古词，加 -age 就成了一个地方。

normal.en: A cottage is smaller than a house and warmer than a tent.
normal.cn: 小屋比房子小，却比帐篷暖和。

normal.en: Think of a low door, a small window and smoke from the chimney.
normal.cn: 想想一扇矮门、一扇小窗和烟囱里的烟。

normal.en: A cottage garden grows flowers beside the vegetables.
normal.cn: 乡舍花园在蔬菜旁边种着花。

normal.en: Cottage and college look alike but live very different lives.
normal.cn: cottage 与 college 长得像，过的却是很不一样的日子。

abstract.en: Picture rain sliding down a roof of yellow straw.
abstract.cn: 想象雨水顺着金黄茅草屋顶滑下。

abstract.en: Picture one warm window in a dark green valley.
abstract.cn: 想象墨绿山谷里的一扇暖窗。

abstract.en: Picture a key too small to open anything but a cottage door.
abstract.cn: 想象一把小得只能开小屋门的钥匙。

examples.en: They spent the summer in a small cottage by the sea.
examples.cn: 他们在海边的一间小屋度过了夏天。

examples.en: We rented a cottage in the hills for a week.
examples.cn: 我们在山里租了一间小屋住了一周。

examples.en: A narrow path leads to the old cottage.
examples.cn: 一条窄路通向那间老屋。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 cottage 记成 cot（小床、小屋）加 tage：一张小床就能安顿下来的地方，就是村舍小屋。

root: 源自古英语 cot（小茅屋、棚舍），中世纪加法语词尾 -age，本指乡间劳动者的小住所，后泛指村舍与度假小屋。

sensesIntro.en: From a worker's small house in the country, to a small house rented for a few weeks.
sensesIntro.cn: 从乡间劳动者的小住所，到租来住几周的小屋。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a stone cottage with a low thatched roof and thin smoke.
core.cn: 核心意象：石头小屋，低矮的茅草顶上升起一缕细烟。

branches.en: A country family lives close to the ground and the weather.
branches.cn: 乡间人家贴着土地与天气生活。

branches.en: A visitor borrows that small life for a short time.
branches.cn: 来客短暂地借用那种小日子。

branches.en: Both are small roofs, one lived in and one borrowed.
branches.cn: 两者都是小屋顶，一个常住，一个借用。

branches.en: The garden and the chimney are part of its picture.
branches.cn: 花园与烟囱都是它画面的一部分。

branches.en: Holiday cottages keep old shapes for new guests.
branches.cn: 度假小屋用旧形状迎接新客人。

intro.en: Cottage joins the old base cot, a hut, with the French noun ending -age, meaning a place.
intro.cn: cottage 由古词基 cot（小屋）加法语名词词尾 -age（场所）构成。

latinIntro.en: The dwelling base cot- also appears in cot, cote and cottage.
latinIntro.cn: 表示住所的词基 cot- 也出现在 cot、cote 与 cottage 中。

items.meaning: a person who lives in a cottage

items.exampleCN: 住小屋的人在门口挥手。

items.meaning: work done at home in small units

items.exampleCN: 织布最初是家庭手工业。

items.meaning: soft white cheese made at home

The cottage garden smell of roses.
items.exampleCN: 乡舍花园里有玫瑰的香气。

items.meaning: a dish of meat under mashed potato

items.exampleCN: 她烤了一个肉馅土豆饼。

items.meaning: a small simple bed or hut
items.example: A cot stood by the wall.

definition_en: the soft white fibre of a plant, the cloth made from it, or thread spun from it
core_image: 枝头绽开一团白云似的棉絮，手指一捏就散成细丝
scene: 老妇人把一团白软的纤维捻成线，一圈圈绕在木轴上。She wore a plain cotton shirt to the market.
sceneCN: 这里 cotton 指「棉布」（第 2 个义项：用棉花织成的布）；句意是她穿着朴素的棉布衬衫去市场。

senses.title: The plant fibre
senses.definition: the soft white fibre that grows around the seeds of a tall plant
senses.definitionCN: 长在高大植物种子周围的柔软白色纤维
senses.example: The fields were white with cotton.
senses.exampleCN: 田野被棉花染成一片白。
senses.why: A plant wraps its seeds in white and humans borrow that coat.
senses.whyCN: 植物给种子裹上白色外衣，人类借用了这层衣服。

senses.title: The woven cloth
senses.definition: cloth made from cotton fibre
senses.definitionCN: 用棉花纤维织成的布
senses.example: She wore a plain cotton shirt to the market.
senses.exampleCN: 她穿着朴素的棉布衬衫去市场。
senses.why: Soft fibre becomes strong cloth when threads cross.
senses.whyCN: 柔软的纤维在经纬交错时变成结实的布。

senses.title: The spun thread
senses.definition: thread made by twisting cotton fibres together
senses.definitionCN: 把棉花纤维捻在一起做成的线
senses.example: The needle needs a length of cotton.
senses.exampleCN: 针上需要一段棉线。
senses.why: Twist a cloud of fibre and it becomes a line you can sew with.
senses.whyCN: 把一团纤维一捻，就成了能缝东西的线。

intro.en: Cotton comes from Arabic qutn, which passed through Italian cotone and Old French coton into English.
intro.cn: cotton 来自阿拉伯语 qutn，经意大利语 cotone 与古法语 coton 进入英语。

items.en: Qutn named the cotton plant and its fibre.
items.cn: qutn 指棉花这种植物及其纤维。

items.en: Cotone carried the word into Mediterranean trade.
items.cn: cotone 把这个词带进地中海贸易。

items.en: Coton named both the fibre and the cloth.
items.cn: coton 既指纤维，也指棉布。

items.en: English cotton first meant the imported cloth.
items.cn: 英语 cotton 最初指进口的棉布。

items.en: It now covers the plant, the fibre, the thread and the cloth.
items.cn: 今天它涵盖植株、纤维、棉线与棉布。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words with a doubled consonant, and the meaning group names other textile words.
note.cn: 形近组收集含双写辅音的单词，近义组列出其他纺织相关的说法。

entries.definition: a box made of thick paper
a stick of coloured wax for drawing
a small round fastener on clothes

woven material used for making things

normalIntro.en: These hooks start with a white ball on a branch, then move to a shirt and to a needle's thread.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从枝头一团白絮开始，再到一件衬衫，最后到针上的棉线。

normal.en: Cotton looks like a small cloud that grew on a stem.
normal.cn: cotton 像一朵长在茎上的小云。

normal.en: The same word is the plant, the fibre, the thread and the shirt.
normal.cn: 同一个词既是植株，也是纤维、棉线和衬衫。

normal.en: Cotton is uncountable, so you say a cotton shirt, not a cotton.
normal.cn: cotton 不可数，所以要说 a cotton shirt，而不是 a cotton。

normal.en: Pick cotton by hand and your fingers learn the word.
normal.cn: 用手采一次棉花，手指就记住了这个词。

normal.en: Two t letters sit in the middle like two bolls on one stem.
normal.cn: 中间两个 t，像同一根茎上的两个棉铃。

abstract.en: Picture a field turning white overnight.
abstract.cn: 想象一片田野一夜之间变白。

abstract.en: Picture a thread pulled from a cloud.
abstract.cn: 想象从一朵云里抽出一根线。

abstract.en: Picture a shirt breathing in a warm wind.
abstract.cn: 想象一件衬衫在暖风里轻轻呼吸。

examples.en: The fields were white with cotton.
examples.cn: 田野被棉花染成一片白。

examples.en: She wore a plain cotton shirt to the market.
examples.cn: 她穿着朴素的棉布衬衫去市场。

examples.en: The needle needs a length of cotton.
examples.cn: 针上需要一段棉线。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 cotton 记成「扣疼」：棉布衬衫的扣子扣得太紧，会勒得人有点疼。

root: 源自阿拉伯语 qutn（棉花），经意大利语 cotone 与古法语 coton 进入英语，本指棉纤维与棉布。

sensesIntro.en: From fibre around a seed, to cloth on a back, and at last to the thin line that holds a button.
sensesIntro.cn: 从种子周围的纤维，到身上的布，最后到缝住纽扣的细线。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a white boll of cotton opening on a dry stem.
core.cn: 核心意象：干枯茎上绽开的一团白棉。

branches.en: The plant gives a soft white coat around its seeds.
branches.cn: 植物在种子周围长出一层柔软的白衣。

branches.en: Crossed threads turn that coat into cloth.
branches.cn: 交错的线把那层衣服变成布。

branches.en: A twisted few fibres become a line for sewing.
branches.cn: 几根纤维一捻，就成了缝东西的线。

branches.en: Fibre and cloth are the same material at two stages.
branches.cn: 纤维与布是同一材料的前后两个阶段。

branches.en: Cloth and thread both begin as a white ball in a field.
branches.cn: 布与线都始于田里的一团白。

intro.en: Cotton is a borrowed base word from Arabic, extended by English compounds and suffixes.
intro.cn: cotton 是从阿拉伯语借来的词根词，再由英语复合与词尾扩展。

latinIntro.en: Though not Latin, the word travelled with cloth trade through Italy and France.
latinIntro.cn: 它虽非拉丁语，却随布匹贸易经过意大利与法国一路旅行。

items.meaning: the seed of the cotton plant

items.exampleCN: 一棵棉白杨为院子遮阴。

items.example: She wiped the cut with cotton wool.
The cotton field stretched for miles.

items.meaning: a factory that spins or weaves cotton
