items.example: Use cotton thread for this cloth.

definition_en: to push air out of the throat with a sudden noise, or the act and sound of doing so
core_image: 一只手捂住嘴，肩膀猛地一抖，胸腔里冲出一声短促的气流
scene: 教室里很安静，后排有人捂着嘴压抑地咳了两声。He coughed softly and looked down at his book.
sceneCN: 这里 cough 指「咳嗽」（第 1 个义项：把气从喉间猛地咳出）；句意是他轻轻咳了一声，低头看自己的书。

senses.title: To push air out sharply
senses.definition: to force air out of the throat with a sudden loud noise
senses.definitionCN: 突然发出响声把气从喉间逼出
senses.example: He coughed softly and looked down at his book.
senses.exampleCN: 他轻轻咳了一声，低头看自己的书。
senses.why: The body uses a burst of air to sweep the throat clean.
senses.whyCN: 身体用一股爆发的气流把喉咙扫干净。

senses.title: The sound and the illness
senses.definition: the act or sound of coughing, or an illness that makes you cough
senses.definitionCN: 咳嗽的动作或声音，或引起咳嗽的病症
senses.example: She has a bad cough and a sore throat.
senses.exampleCN: 她咳嗽得厉害，嗓子也疼。
senses.why: One short sound can name both the act and the sickness behind it.
senses.whyCN: 一声短响，既能指动作，也能指背后的病。

senses.title: To bring something up
senses.definition: to clear something from the throat or lungs by coughing
senses.definitionCN: 通过咳嗽把喉间或肺里的东西排出
senses.example: He coughed up a bit of dust.
senses.exampleCN: 他咳出一点灰尘。
senses.why: The burst of air carries what the body wants gone.
senses.whyCN: 那股爆发的气流带走了身体想丢掉的东西。

intro.en: Cough is an imitative word: its sound echoes the noise it names, and it has been spelled many ways.
intro.cn: cough 是一个拟声词，读音模仿它所指的声音，历史上拼法变过许多次。

items.en: A word close to cohhian described noisy throat clearing.
items.cn: 接近 cohhian 的古词形容响亮地清嗓。

items.en: Coughen became the usual verb for the act.
items.cn: coughen 成为表示这一动作的常用动词。

items.en: The noun named both the sound and the sickness.
items.cn: 名词既指声音，也指病症。

items.en: The modern spelling settled while the sound stayed rough.
items.cn: 现代拼法固定下来，读音却依旧粗粝。

items.en: It now also means to force something out, as in cough up money.
items.cn: 今天它也指把东西逼出来，如 cough up money。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the -ough spelling, and the meaning group names other noisy throat actions.
note.cn: 形近组共享 -ough 拼写，近义组列出其他喉间发声的动作。

entries.definition: not smooth to the touch
strong and hard to break
a main branch of a tree
to cough in short dry bursts
to breathe with a whistling sound
to clear the throat noisily

normalIntro.en: These hooks start with a hand over the mouth, then move to a winter illness and to dust leaving the throat.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从一只手捂住嘴开始，再到一场冬季的病，最后到被咳出的灰尘。

normal.en: The spelling is rough, just like the sound it makes.
normal.cn: 这个拼法很粗粝，正像它发出的声音。

normal.en: Cough, though and rough all hide the same odd ending.
normal.cn: cough、though 与 rough 都藏着同样古怪的词尾。

normal.en: A dry cough has no reward; a chest cough brings something up.
normal.cn: 干咳没有结果，胸咳会带出东西。

normal.en: If you cough up money, you pay it unwillingly.
normal.cn: 如果说 cough up money，就是不情愿地掏钱。

normal.en: The past tense doubles nothing: coughed, coughed.
normal.cn: 过去式不双写：coughed、coughed。

abstract.en: Picture a small cloud of dust leaving a doorway.
abstract.cn: 想象一小团灰尘从门口冲出。

abstract.en: Picture a hand pressed hard against a mouth in a quiet room.
abstract.cn: 想象安静的房间里，一只手紧紧捂住嘴。

abstract.en: Picture a chest rising once and then falling still.
abstract.cn: 想象胸腔猛地一鼓，随后又静下来。

examples.en: He coughed softly and looked down at his book.
examples.cn: 他轻轻咳了一声，低头看自己的书。

examples.en: She has a bad cough and a sore throat.
examples.cn: 她咳嗽得厉害，嗓子也疼。

examples.en: He coughed up a bit of dust.
examples.cn: 他咳出一点灰尘。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 cough 记成「口扶」：咳嗽时用手扶住口鼻，读音也像短促的一声。

root: 源自古英语中表示清嗓声的拟声词，经中古英语 coughen 定型，读音模仿喉间突然冲出的气流。

sensesIntro.en: From a burst of air, to the illness it signals, and at last to what that burst carries out.
sensesIntro.cn: 从一股冲出的气，到它所暗示的病症，最后到那股气带出来的东西。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand over the mouth and a shoulder that jerks once.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手捂住嘴，肩膀猛地一抖。

branches.en: The body fires one quick shot of air.
branches.cn: 身体射出一发短促的空气子弹。

branches.en: The same sound also names the sickness that repeats it.
branches.cn: 同一个声音也指让它反复出现的病。

branches.en: Whatever blocked the throat leaves with the blast.
branches.cn: 堵在喉间的东西随那股气流离开。

branches.en: The act and the illness wear one name.
branches.cn: 动作与病症共用一个名字。

branches.en: A cough both clears the way and shows what was in it.
branches.cn: 咳嗽既清出通道，也显露出里面有什么。

intro.en: Cough is a sound word that takes regular endings and forms compounds with medicine and drop.
intro.cn: cough 是拟声词，可加规则词尾，也能与 medicine、drop 组成复合词。

latinIntro.en: This word has no Latin root; its shape follows the noise, not a stem.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有拉丁词根，它的形状跟随声音，而不是跟随词干。

items.example: Do not cough on the food.
The cougher sat at the back.

items.meaning: liquid or pills for a cough
a sweet tablet for a sore throat
sweet thick liquid for a cough
items.example: The cough syrup helped a little.
items.exampleCN: 止咳糖浆起了一点作用。

definition_en: the past form of can, used for past ability, for possibility, or for a polite request
core_image: 一个孩子仰头看树，脚尖一蹬就够到了最高的枝
scene: 孩子盯着树上的风筝，跳了两次还是够不着。When I was young, I could climb that tree in seconds.
sceneCN: 这里 could 指「能够」（第 1 个义项：过去有能力做某事）；句意是我小时候几秒钟就能爬上那棵树。

derivatives.zh: 将会；愿意（相关情态动词）

senses.title: Past ability
senses.definition: used as the past form of can to say that someone was able to do something
senses.definitionCN: 作为 can 的过去式，表示某人过去有能力做某事
senses.example: When I was young, I could climb that tree in seconds.
senses.exampleCN: 我小时候几秒钟就能爬上那棵树。
senses.why: Memory keeps a door open to strength we no longer have.
senses.whyCN: 记忆为那份已不再有的力气留着一扇门。

senses.title: What is possible
senses.definition: used to say that something is possible, though not certain
senses.definitionCN: 用于表示某事有可能，但不确定
senses.example: The keys could be in your coat.
senses.exampleCN: 钥匙可能在你大衣里。
senses.why: A door left a little open lets many futures through.
senses.whyCN: 一扇虚掩的门，能让许多种未来通过。

senses.title: A polite request
senses.definition: used to ask for something or to make a suggestion politely
senses.definitionCN: 用于礼貌地提出请求或建议
senses.example: Could you close the window, please?
senses.exampleCN: 请你把窗关上好吗？
senses.why: Softening the voice is how English opens a door without pushing.
senses.whyCN: 把语气放软，是英语不推门也能让门打开的方式。

intro.en: Could began as the past tense of can; its l was later added by writers who copied would and should.
intro.cn: could 原本是 can 的过去式，后来人们仿照 would 与 should 给它补上了一个 l。

items.en: Cunnan meant to know or to know how.
items.cn: cunnan 意为知道或懂得如何做。

items.en: Cuþe was the past form, meaning knew how.
items.cn: cuþe 是它的过去式，意为当时懂得如何做。

items.en: Coude carried the sense of past ability.
items.cn: coude 带着过去能力的意思继续使用。

items.en: An l was inserted to match would and should.
items.cn: 为了与 would、should 一致，词中插入了字母 l。

items.en: It now also marks possibility and polite requests.
items.cn: 今天它也用来表示可能性与礼貌请求。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers modals and one similar noun, and the meaning group names other modals of ability and possibility.
note.cn: 形近组收集情态动词与一个形近名词，近义组列出其他表示能力与可能的情态动词。

entries.definition: used for habits or imagined situations
entries.definitionCN: 用于习惯或想象的情形

entries.definition: used for duty or advice
a white or grey mass in the sky
entries.definitionCN: 天空中白色或灰色的团块

entries.definition: to be able to do something
used to say something is possible
used for possibility or permission

normalIntro.en: These hooks start with a child in a tree, then move to lost keys and to a politely closed window.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从树上的孩子开始，再到找不到的钥匙，最后到一扇被礼貌关上的窗。

normal.en: Could is can wearing a past tense coat.
normal.cn: could 就是 can 披上一件过去时的外衣。

normal.en: The l is silent but it links could to would and should.
normal.cn: l 不发音，却把 could 与 would、should 连在一起。

normal.en: Could is softer than can, so requests sound lighter.
normal.cn: could 比 can 更软，所以请求听起来更轻。

normal.en: Could be means the door is open but nobody has walked in.
normal.cn: could be 表示门开着，但还没人走进来。

normal.en: Could have done points at a past that never happened.
normal.cn: could have done 指向一个从未发生的过去。

abstract.en: Picture a hand reaching a fruit one branch too high.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手伸向高出一截的果子。

abstract.en: Picture several doors open at once in a dark hall.
abstract.cn: 想象昏暗走廊里同时开着好几扇门。

abstract.en: Picture a request written in soft pencil, not ink.
abstract.cn: 想象一个用铅笔而不是墨水写下的请求。

examples.en: When I was young, I could climb that tree in seconds.
examples.cn: 我小时候几秒钟就能爬上那棵树。

examples.en: The keys could be in your coat.
examples.cn: 钥匙可能在你大衣里。

examples.en: Could you close the window, please?
examples.cn: 请你把窗关上好吗？

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 could 记成 can 的过去式加一个不发音的 l：能力退到过去，语气也变得温和。

root: 源自古英语 cunnan（知道、懂得如何做）的过去式 cuþe，中古英语作 coude，十六世纪仿 would、should 插入 l 定型。

sensesIntro.en: From strength remembered, to a possibility left open, and at last to a request made gentle.
sensesIntro.cn: 从记忆中的力气，到留着的可能性，最后到被放软的请求。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a child reaching a high branch with ease.
core.cn: 核心意象：孩子轻松够到高高的树枝。

branches.en: Past strength is remembered as a fact.
branches.cn: 过去的力气被当作事实记住。

branches.en: One possible answer is left on the table.
branches.cn: 一种可能的答案被留在桌上。

branches.en: A request is offered with room to refuse.
branches.cn: 请求被提出时，还留着拒绝的余地。

branches.en: Both loosen certainty, one about the past and one about now.
branches.cn: 两者都放松了确定性，一个关于过去，一个关于现在。

branches.en: Possibility and politeness both keep a door slightly open.
branches.cn: 可能性与礼貌都把门留了一条缝。

intro.en: Could is a closed modal form; it changes for nothing and joins only with not or have.
intro.cn: could 是封闭的情态形式，本身不变形，只能与 not 或 have 组合。

latinIntro.en: The word is native English, not Latin, and keeps the old past ending.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词是英语本族词，并非拉丁语，保留着古老的过去式词尾。

items.meaning: might have done in the past
future in the past or a wish
having the power to do something

definition_zh: 委员会；理事会；地方议会；会议
definition_en: a group of people chosen to make decisions or give advice, especially for a town or organisation
core_image: 一张圆桌旁围坐着被推选出来的人，举手决定一件事
scene: 会议室里十二个人围坐一圈，举手表决是否修那条路。The city council voted to repair the old road.
sceneCN: 这里 council 指「地方议会」（第 2 个义项：管理城镇事务的议事机构）；句意是市议会投票决定修那条旧路。

pos.zh: 委员会；理事会；地方议会；会议

senses.title: A chosen decision group
senses.definition: a group of people chosen to make decisions or give advice
senses.definitionCN: 被推选出来做决定或提建议的一群人
senses.example: The arts council gave the theatre a grant.
senses.exampleCN: 艺术委员会给了这家剧院一笔拨款。
senses.why: Many voices need one table to become one decision.
senses.whyCN: 许多声音需要一张桌子，才能变成一个决定。

senses.title: The body that runs a town
senses.definition: the group that governs a town or local area
senses.definitionCN: 管理一座城镇或地方区域的机构
senses.example: The city council voted to repair the old road.
senses.exampleCN: 市议会投票决定修那条旧路。
senses.why: A town is too large for one desk, so it borrows a table of many.
senses.whyCN: 一座城一张桌子管不过来，于是借来一张多人的桌子。

senses.title: A meeting for advice
senses.definition: a formal meeting held to discuss and advise on a matter
senses.definitionCN: 为讨论并议定某事而召开的正式会议
senses.example: The generals held a council before dawn.
senses.exampleCN: 将军们在黎明前开了一次军事会议。
senses.why: Before a hard act comes a room where words are weighed.
senses.whyCN: 艰难行动之前，总有一间称量话语的屋子。

intro.en: Council comes from Latin concilium, a calling together, from com-, together, and calare, to call.
intro.cn: council 来自拉丁语 concilium（召集到一起），由 com-（一起）与 calare（呼喊、召集）构成。

items.en: Calare meant to call or summon.
items.cn: calare 意为呼喊或召集。

items.en: Concilium named a body called together for advice.
items.cn: concilium 指为商议而被召集起来的团体。

items.en: Concile meant an assembly or a meeting.
items.cn: concile 意为集会或会议。

items.en: English council named a group that advises a ruler.
items.cn: 英语 council 指为统治者出主意的团体。

items.en: It now names town bodies, committees and formal meetings.
items.cn: 今天它指市政机构、委员会与正式会议。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the easily confused council, counsel and consul, and the meaning group names other decision groups.
note.cn: 形近组收集易混的 council、counsel 与 consul，近义组列出其他决策团体。

entries.definition: advice, or a lawyer who gives it
entries.definitionCN: 建议，或提供建议的律师

entries.definition: an official living abroad to help citizens
entries.definitionCN: 驻外帮助本国公民的官员

entries.definition: to comfort someone in sadness
a small group chosen for a special task
entries.definitionCN: 为专项任务选出的少数人

entries.definition: the group that directs a company
a group gathered for a shared purpose
entries.definitionCN: 为共同目的聚集的群体

normalIntro.en: These hooks start with a round table of chosen people, then move to a town body and to generals meeting before dawn.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从被推选者的圆桌开始，再到市政机构，最后到黎明前开会的将军们。

normal.en: Council hides the word call: people called together to decide.
normal.cn: council 里藏着 call：被叫到一起做决定的人。

normal.en: Council is the group; counsel is the advice it gives.
normal.cn: council 是团体，counsel 是它给出的建议。

normal.en: A council sits at a round table so no seat looks highest.
normal.cn: 议会坐圆桌，这样没有哪个座位显得最高。

normal.en: City council decides roads, housing and rubbish.
normal.cn: 市议会决定道路、住房与垃圾的事。

normal.en: The ending -il is quiet, but the word means loud debate.
normal.cn: 词尾 -il 很安静，这个词的意思却是喧闹的辩论。

abstract.en: Picture many hands rising in a single room.
abstract.cn: 想象许多只手在同一间屋子里举起。

abstract.en: Picture a round table worn smooth by elbows.
abstract.cn: 想象一张被手肘磨得光滑的圆桌。

abstract.en: Picture a town seen from above as many doors and one table.
abstract.cn: 想象从高处看一座城，许多扇门和一张桌子。

examples.en: The city council voted to repair the old road.
examples.cn: 市议会投票决定修那条旧路。

examples.en: The arts council gave the theatre a grant.
examples.cn: 艺术委员会给了这家剧院一笔拨款。

examples.en: The generals held a council before dawn.
examples.cn: 将军们在黎明前开了一次军事会议。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 council 记成「被 call 到一起的人」：被召集来议事的团体，就是委员会与议会。

root: 源自拉丁语 concilium（集会），由 com-（一起）与 calare（呼喊、召集）构成，本指被召集议事的人，后指委员会与地方议会。

sensesIntro.en: From a group called to advise, to the body that runs a town, and at last to the meeting itself.
sensesIntro.cn: 从被召来出主意的团体，到管理城镇的机构，最后到会议本身。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: chosen people seated around one round table.
core.cn: 核心意象：被推选的人围坐在一张圆桌旁。

branches.en: A chosen group turns talk into advice.
branches.cn: 被选出的团体把谈话变成建议。

branches.en: A town body turns advice into local rules.
branches.cn: 市政机构把建议变成地方规矩。

branches.en: A meeting turns many voices into one plan.
branches.cn: 一场会议把许多声音变成一个方案。

branches.en: Both are bodies with the power to decide.
branches.cn: 两者都是握有决定权的机构。

branches.en: The body and its meeting share one name because the meeting is the body at work.
branches.cn: 机构与会议共用一个名字，因为会议就是机构在工作。

intro.en: Council rests on Latin calare, to call, with com-, together, and the noun shape -ium.
intro.cn: council 建立在拉丁语 calare（呼喊、召集）之上，配 com-（一起）与名词形态 -ium。

latinIntro.en: The calling base cal- also appears in calendar and clamour.
latinIntro.cn: 表示呼喊与召集的词基 cal- 也出现在 calendar 与 clamour 中。

items.example: The councilwoman asked for a vote.

items.meaning: the governing body of a city
homes owned by a local council
items.example: They grew up in council housing.
items.exampleCN: 他们在市政住房里长大。

definition_en: advice given to someone, to give such advice, or a lawyer who speaks for a person in court
core_image: 一位长辈把两条路的利弊摊在桌上，让年轻人自己选
scene: 年轻人想退学，老师没有替他决定，只把利弊一条条摆出来。She counselled him to wait one more term.
sceneCN: 这里 counsel 指「劝告」（第 2 个义项：给出建议而不替人决定）；句意是她劝他再等一个学期。

pos.zh: 忠告；建议；律师；法律顾问

senses.title: Advice from someone wise
senses.definition: careful advice given to someone about what they should do
senses.definitionCN: 就某人该怎么做而给出的慎重建议
senses.example: He sought counsel from his old teacher.
senses.exampleCN: 他向年迈的老师寻求忠告。
senses.why: A second pair of eyes can see the road you cannot.
senses.whyCN: 多一双眼睛，就能看见你看不见的那条路。

senses.title: To advise someone
senses.definition: to give someone advice about a decision or a course of action
senses.definitionCN: 就决定或行动方案向某人提出建议
senses.example: She counselled him to wait one more term.
senses.exampleCN: 她劝他再等一个学期。
senses.why: Advice is a lamp handed over, not a hand that pushes.
senses.whyCN: 劝告是递过去的一盏灯，而不是推人的一只手。

senses.title: A lawyer in court
senses.definition: a lawyer who represents someone in a legal case
senses.definitionCN: 在法律案件中代表某人的律师
senses.example: The defence counsel asked for more time.
senses.exampleCN: 辩护律师请求多给一些时间。
senses.why: In court, advice must stand up and speak aloud.
senses.whyCN: 在法庭上，建议必须站起来大声说话。

intro.en: Counsel comes from Latin consilium, advice or plan, from consulere, to consult or take counsel.
intro.cn: counsel 来自拉丁语 consilium（建议、计划），源自动词 consulere（商议、征询）。

items.en: Consulere meant to consult or ask for advice.
items.cn: consulere 意为商议或征询建议。

items.en: Consilium named a plan or a piece of advice.
items.cn: consilium 指计划或一条建议。

items.en: Conseil kept both the advice and the act of advising.
items.cn: conseil 既指建议，也指提建议这件事。

items.en: English counsel meant advice and the giving of it.
items.cn: 英语 counsel 指建议以及给出建议。

items.en: It also names the lawyer who gives advice in court.
items.cn: 它也表示在法庭上提供建议的律师。

note.en: The look-alike group sets council, consul and console beside counsel, and the meaning group names advice and lawyers.
note.cn: 形近组把 council、consul 与 console 放在 counsel 旁边，近义组列出建议与律师的说法。

entries.definition: a group chosen to make decisions
an official who helps citizens abroad
entries.definitionCN: 在海外帮助本国公民的官员

entries.definition: to comfort a sad person
an opinion about what someone should do
entries.definitionCN: 关于某人该怎么做的一种意见

entries.definition: to tell someone what you think they should do
entries.definitionCN: 告诉某人你认为他该怎么做

entries.definition: a person trained to argue legal cases
entries.definitionCN: 受过训练、办理法律案件的人

normalIntro.en: These hooks start with a lamp passed to a young hand, then move to a gentle warning and to a lawyer standing up in court.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从递到年轻人手里的灯开始，再到一句温和的劝阻，最后到法庭上站起来的律师。

normal.en: Council is the group; counsel is the advice it gives.
normal.cn: council 是团体，counsel 是它给出的建议。

normal.en: The single l points like a lamp toward one path.
normal.cn: 中间的一个 l 像一盏灯，指向一条路。

normal.en: To counsel is to hand over a map and step back.
normal.cn: 劝告就是递过一张地图，然后退后一步。

normal.en: A defence counsel stands between a person and a sentence.
normal.cn: 辩护律师站在一个人与一份判决之间。

normal.en: Keep your own counsel means keep the map in your pocket.
normal.cn: keep your own counsel 就是把地图留在自己口袋里。

abstract.en: Picture two roads drawn on a napkin.
abstract.cn: 想象餐巾纸上画出的两条路。

abstract.en: Picture a hand holding a lamp but not pulling an arm.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手举着灯，却不拉扯别人的手臂。

abstract.en: Picture a quiet voice in a room full of loud choices.
abstract.cn: 想象满是喧闹选择的屋子里，一个安静的声音。

examples.en: She counselled him to wait one more term.
examples.cn: 她劝他再等一个学期。

examples.en: He sought counsel from his old teacher.
examples.cn: 他向年迈的老师寻求忠告。

examples.en: The defence counsel asked for more time.
examples.cn: 辩护律师请求多给一些时间。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 counsel 记成「靠 sell」：好建议不是拿来卖的，而是靠得住的人私下给的忠告。

root: 源自拉丁语 consilium（建议、计划），来自 consulere（商议、征询），本指商议后给出的意见，后也指提供意见的律师。

sensesIntro.en: From a plan offered to a friend, to the act of offering it, and at last to the lawyer who offers it in court.
sensesIntro.cn: 从给朋友的一个方案，到给出方案这一动作，最后到在法庭上给出意见的律师。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two paths laid on a table, with a lamp beside them.
core.cn: 核心意象：桌上摊开两条路，旁边放着一盏灯。

branches.en: A trusted voice names the safer path.
branches.cn: 一个可信的声音指出更稳的那条路。

branches.en: The act of advising leaves the choice where it belongs.
branches.cn: 劝告这一动作，把选择留在该在的人手里。

branches.en: In court the advice becomes a public argument.
branches.cn: 在法庭上，建议变成公开的辩论。

branches.en: The noun and the verb name one act from two sides.
branches.cn: 名词与动词从两侧说同一个动作。

branches.en: A lawyer also counsels a client, but with the law at hand.
branches.cn: 律师也在劝告当事人，只是手里多了一部法律。

intro.en: Counsel is a base word from Latin consilium, with English endings for the person and the activity.
intro.cn: counsel 是源自拉丁语 consilium 的词根词，再由英语词尾派生出人物与活动。

latinIntro.en: The consulting base consul- also appears in consult, consultation and consul.
latinIntro.cn: 表示商议的词基 consul- 也出现在 consult、consultation 与 consul 中。

definition_en: to say numbers in order or find how many there are, to matter, or the total reached
core_image: 一只手指数过一排豆子，指尖一停就得出总数
scene: 孩子闭着眼，一只一只数着藏起来的小伙伴。She counted to ten before she opened her eyes.
sceneCN: 这里 count 指「数数」（第 1 个义项：按顺序说出数目）；句意是她数到十才睁开眼睛。

senses.title: To say numbers or find a total
senses.definition: to say numbers in order, or to find how many things there are
senses.definitionCN: 按顺序说出数字，或查明有多少个事物
senses.example: She counted to ten before she opened her eyes.
senses.exampleCN: 她数到十才睁开眼睛。
senses.why: A finger moving from object to object turns a crowd into a number.
senses.whyCN: 手指从一件东西移到另一件，人群就变成一个数。

senses.title: To matter
senses.definition: to have importance or value
senses.definitionCN: 具有重要性或价值
senses.example: Every vote counts in a small town.
senses.exampleCN: 在小镇上，每一票都重要。
senses.why: What is counted is noticed, and what is noticed has weight.
senses.whyCN: 被数到的东西才被看见，被看见的才有分量。

senses.title: The total reached
senses.definition: the number reached by counting, or the act of counting
senses.definitionCN: 数出来的数目，或数数这一行为
senses.example: The final count was three hundred.
senses.exampleCN: 最后的计数是三百。
senses.why: Counting ends by placing a single number on the table.
senses.whyCN: 数数最后，总要把一个数字放到桌上。

intro.en: Count comes from Latin computare, to reckon, through Old French conter, to tell or count.
intro.cn: count 来自拉丁语 computare（计算），经古法语 conter（讲述、计数）进入英语。

items.en: Computare meant to reckon or add up.
items.cn: computare 意为计算或合计。

items.en: Computus named a reckoning or an account.
items.cn: computus 指一次计算或一本账。

items.en: Conter meant to tell a story or count items.
items.cn: conter 意为讲述故事或清点物品。

items.en: English count named the act of numbering.
items.cn: 英语 count 指数数这一动作。

items.en: It also means to matter, as in every second counts.
items.cn: 它也表示重要，如 every second counts。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words near count in shape, and the meaning group names other words for numbering and mattering.
note.cn: 形近组收集形状接近 count 的词，近义组列出其他表示计数与重要的说法。

entries.definition: a local area with its own government
entries.definitionCN: 拥有本地政府的一级地方区域

to climb onto something

normalIntro.en: These hooks start with a finger over beans, then move to a vote that matters and to a final total.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从指点豆子的手指开始，再到重要的一票，最后到最终的总数。

normal.en: Count is the sound of one finger tapping each thing.
normal.cn: count 就是一根手指点过每件东西的声音。

normal.en: Counting ends with one number standing alone.
normal.cn: 数到最后，总有一个数字独自站着。

normal.en: If something counts, it is worth counting.
normal.cn: 如果某件事 counts，它就值得被数进去。

normal.en: Count on someone means you can put them in your total.
normal.cn: count on 某人，就是能把他算进你的总数。

normal.en: Keep the ou sound: count, not cant.
normal.cn: 记住 ou 的读音：count，不是 cant。

abstract.en: Picture beans sliding from a pile into a line.
abstract.cn: 想象豆子从一堆滑成一行。

abstract.en: Picture a hand raised in a hall of raised hands.
abstract.cn: 想象满堂举起的手中，有一只被算进去。

abstract.en: Picture a total written at the bottom of a long page.
abstract.cn: 想象长页底部写下的一个总数。

examples.en: She counted to ten before she opened her eyes.
examples.cn: 她数到十才睁开眼睛。

examples.en: Every vote counts in a small town.
examples.cn: 在小镇上，每一票都重要。

examples.en: The final count was three hundred.
examples.cn: 最后的计数是三百。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 count 记成「靠数」：一件事靠得住地数清楚，才知道它到底重不重要。

root: 源自拉丁语 computare（计算、合计），经古法语 conter（讲述、计数）进入英语，本指清点数目，后引申为有价值、重要。

sensesIntro.en: From a finger moving over objects, to a vote with weight, and at last to the one number left on the page.
sensesIntro.cn: 从手指移过物件，到有分量的一票，最后到纸上留下的那个数字。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a finger moving along a row of beans.
core.cn: 核心意象：一根手指沿着一排豆子移动。

branches.en: The finger turns many things into one number.
branches.cn: 手指把许多东西变成一个数。

branches.en: Being included in the count gives a thing weight.
branches.cn: 被算进数目，就给了某件事分量。

branches.en: The total is the counting laid flat on paper.
branches.cn: 总数就是摊在纸上的数数结果。

branches.en: The act and its result share one short word.
branches.cn: 动作与结果共用一个短词。

branches.en: What is counted matters, and what matters is counted.
branches.cn: 被数的才重要，重要的才会被数。

intro.en: Count is a base verb from Latin computare, to reckon, with many English suffixes and compounds.
intro.cn: count 是源自拉丁语 computare（计算）的词根动词，英语中派生与复合都很多。

latinIntro.en: The reckoning base put- also appears in compute, computer and reputation.
latinIntro.cn: 表示计算的词基 put- 也出现在 compute、computer 与 reputation 中。

items.meaning: a device or place for counting
items.meaningCN: 用于计数的器具或场所

items.meaning: a record or explanation of money
items.meaningCN: 关于钱财的记录或说明

definition_en: a long table where customers are served, a device that counts, or to speak or act against something
core_image: 一道长长的台面把顾客与货物分开，钱在台面上来回
scene: 售货员隔着玻璃台面递出车票，乘客把钱放进小托盘。She paid at the counter and took her ticket.
sceneCN: 这里 counter 指「柜台」（第 1 个义项：商店或车站办理业务的长台）；句意是她在柜台付了钱，拿走了车票。

senses.title: The serving table
senses.definition: a long flat table in a shop, bank or station where customers are served
senses.definitionCN: 商店、银行或车站中接待顾客的长台
senses.example: She paid at the counter and took her ticket.
senses.exampleCN: 她在柜台付了钱，拿走了车票。
senses.why: A flat board is all that stands between a wish and a price.
senses.whyCN: 一块平平的台面，就是愿望与价格之间的全部距离。

senses.title: To speak against
senses.definition: to reply to an argument or action in order to oppose it
senses.definitionCN: 为反对某论点或行动而作出回应
senses.example: She countered his claim with a single fact.
senses.exampleCN: 她用一个事实反驳了他的说法。
senses.why: A blow can be answered by a blow that lands first.
senses.whyCN: 一拳打来，可以用先落下的一拳回应。

senses.title: A counting device
senses.definition: a small device or dial that records a number
senses.definitionCN: 记录数字的小装置或刻度盘
senses.example: The counter clicked past nine hundred.
senses.exampleCN: 计数器咔哒一声越过了九百。
senses.why: A machine counts so that a hand does not have to.
senses.whyCN: 机器来数，手就不必数了。

intro.en: Counter comes from Old French comptoir, a counting desk, from conter, to count, and Latin computare, to reckon.
intro.cn: counter 来自古法语 comptoir（算账的台子），源自 conter（计数）与拉丁语 computare（计算）。

items.en: Computare meant to reckon or add up.
items.cn: computare 意为计算或合计。

items.en: Conter meant to count or tell.
items.cn: conter 意为计数或讲述。

items.en: Comptoir named the desk where money was counted.
items.cn: comptoir 指数钱的台子。

items.en: English counter first named a shop table for money.
items.cn: 英语 counter 最初指商店里处理钱款的台子。

items.en: It now also means a counting device and a verbal reply against something.
items.cn: 今天它也指计数器，以及针对某事的言语回应。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the counting base count-, and the meaning group names other words for opposing and for a sales point.
note.cn: 形近组共享表示计数的词基 count-，近义组列出其他表示反对与售货点的说法。

entries.definitionCN: 用于服务或展示的小隔间

normalIntro.en: These hooks start with a long serving table, then move to a verbal answer and to a small clicking device.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从一张长柜台开始，再到一句口头回击，最后到咔哒作响的小装置。

normal.en: A counter was once a desk for counting money, so the table keeps the name.
normal.cn: counter 原本是数钱的台子，所以柜台沿用了这个名字。

normal.en: To counter is to put a word on the other side of the scale.
normal.cn: 反驳就是把一句话放到天平的另一边。

normal.en: Over the counter medicine needs no prescription.
normal.cn: 柜台药不需要处方。

normal.en: Count plus -er gives both a person who counts and a thing that counts.
normal.cn: count 加 -er，既可以是数数的人，也可以是计数的东西。

normal.en: Counter- at the front of a word means against, as in counterattack.
normal.cn: 词首的 counter- 表示反对，如 counterattack。

abstract.en: Picture a glass top with coins on one side and goods on the other.
abstract.cn: 想象一块玻璃台面，一边是钱，一边是货。

abstract.en: Picture two arrows meeting head to head.
abstract.cn: 想象两支箭头头顶头撞在一起。

abstract.en: Picture a small wheel turning one tooth at a time.
abstract.cn: 想象一个小轮子一次转过一格。

examples.en: She paid at the counter and took her ticket.
examples.cn: 她在柜台付了钱，拿走了车票。

examples.en: She countered his claim with a single fact.
examples.cn: 她用一个事实反驳了他的说法。

examples.en: The counter clicked past nine hundred.
examples.cn: 计数器咔哒一声越过了九百。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 counter 记成 count（数）加 er：数钱数货的地方就是柜台，反过来顶回去就是反驳。

root: 源自拉丁语 computare（计算），经古法语 conter（计数）与 comptoir（算账台）进入英语，本指数钱的台子，后引申为计数器与反驳。

sensesIntro.en: From a table where money is counted, to a reply that counts against a claim, and at last to a device that counts alone.
sensesIntro.cn: 从数钱的台子，到针对某说法的回击，最后到独自计数的装置。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a long flat counter with goods on one side and money on the other.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张长柜台，一边是货，一边是钱。

branches.en: The counter holds the exchange between buyer and seller.
branches.cn: 柜台承载买卖双方之间的交换。

branches.en: A reply pushes back against a claim.
branches.cn: 一句回应把某个说法顶回去。

branches.en: A device keeps the total without a human hand.
branches.cn: 装置不用人手就能记住总数。

branches.en: Both are places or things where counting happens.
branches.cn: 两者都是发生计数的地方或物件。

branches.en: To counter and to count both weigh one thing against another.
branches.cn: 反驳与计数，都是把一物与另一物相衡量。

intro.en: Counter is count plus -er, giving a person, a place or a device connected with counting.
intro.cn: counter 由 count 加 -er 构成，表示与计数有关的人、场所或装置。

latinIntro.en: The prefix counter- also means against, as in counteract and counterattack.
latinIntro.cn: 前缀 counter- 也表示反对，如 counteract 与 counterattack。

definition_en: a nation with its own government, the land outside towns, or the territory of a nation
core_image: 一条国界线在地图上弯过山脊，线内是田野、道路与人家
scene: 车开出城后，两边是麦田和矮山，空气里有草的味道。They moved to the country to grow vegetables.
sceneCN: 这里 country 指「乡村」（第 2 个义项：城市之外的农村地区）；句意是他们搬到乡下种菜。

senses.title: A nation with a government
senses.definition: a nation with its own government, borders and people
senses.definitionCN: 拥有自己政府、边界与人民的国家
senses.example: The country has three official languages.
senses.exampleCN: 这个国家有三种官方语言。
senses.why: A line on a map gathers millions of lives under one name.
senses.whyCN: 地图上的一条线，把千万人的生活收在一个名字下。

senses.title: The land outside towns
senses.definition: the countryside, away from cities and large towns
senses.definitionCN: 远离城市与大镇的农村地区
senses.example: They moved to the country to grow vegetables.
senses.exampleCN: 他们搬到乡下种菜。
senses.why: Where houses thin out, fields and slow roads take over.
senses.whyCN: 房子稀了，田野与慢路便接过了地盘。

senses.title: The land itself
senses.definition: the territory and natural land of a nation
senses.definitionCN: 一个国家的疆域与自然土地
senses.example: The north of the country is cold and dry.
senses.exampleCN: 这个国家的北部寒冷干燥。
senses.why: A nation is also soil, rivers and weather.
senses.whyCN: 一个国家也是土壤、河流与天气。

intro.en: Country comes from Old French contrée, from Latin terra contrata, the land lying opposite or facing you.
intro.cn: country 来自古法语 contrée，源自拉丁语 terra contrata（对面展开的土地）。

items.en: Contra meant opposite or facing.
items.cn: contra 意为在对面、面向。

items.en: Terra contrata named the land spread out before a viewer.
items.cn: terra contrata 指在观看者面前铺开的土地。

items.en: Contree meant a region or a district.
items.cn: contree 意为一片地区或区域。

items.en: English country named a land or a rural area.
items.cn: 英语 country 指国土或乡村地区。

items.en: It now covers the nation, its land and the land outside towns.
items.cn: 今天它涵盖国家、国土与城镇之外的乡野。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the count- shape, and the meaning group names other words for a nation and its land.
note.cn: 形近组共享 count- 的形状，近义组列出其他表示国家与土地的说法。

entries.definition: a local area smaller than a country
entries.definitionCN: 比国家小的地方行政区

normalIntro.en: These hooks start with a line on a map, then move to fields outside town and to the soil of a nation.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从地图上的一条线开始，再到城外的田野，最后到一个国家的土地。

normal.en: Country is the land spread out in front of you.
normal.cn: country 就是在你面前铺开的那片土地。

normal.en: The word covers both the nation and the fields beyond the last house.
normal.cn: 这个词既指国家，也指最后一栋房子之外的田野。

normal.en: In the country means among fields, not among flags.
normal.cn: in the country 是指在田野之间，而不是在旗帜之间。

normal.en: The plural changes y to ies: countries.
normal.cn: 复数把 y 变成 ies：countries。

normal.en: Country music sounds like a road with no city at the end.
normal.cn: 乡村音乐听起来像一条尽头没有城市的路。

abstract.en: Picture a border line following a mountain ridge.
abstract.cn: 想象一条国界线沿着山脊延伸。

abstract.en: Picture wheat moving in waves beside a narrow road.
abstract.cn: 想象窄路旁麦浪起伏。

abstract.en: Picture a flag and a field sharing the same light.
abstract.cn: 想象一面旗与一片田共享同一片光。

examples.en: They moved to the country to grow vegetables.
examples.cn: 他们搬到乡下种菜。

examples.en: The country has three official languages.
examples.cn: 这个国家有三种官方语言。

examples.en: The north of the country is cold and dry.
examples.cn: 这个国家的北部寒冷干燥。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 country 记成「看 tree」：一眼望去全是田野和树的地方，就是乡村，也是一个国家。

root: 源自拉丁语 terra contrata（对面铺开的土地），由 contra（在对面）与 terra（土地）构成，经古法语 contrée 进入英语。

sensesIntro.en: From a nation under one government, to the fields outside town, and at last to the soil itself.
sensesIntro.cn: 从同一个政府下的国家，到城外的田野，最后到土地本身。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a border line bending along a ridge, with fields inside it.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条国界线沿山脊弯曲，线内是田野。

branches.en: A government and a border make a nation.
branches.cn: 一个政府与一条边界，构成一个国家。

branches.en: Beyond the last street, fields take the place of shops.
branches.cn: 最后一条街之外，田野取代了店铺。

branches.en: The land itself has weather, rivers and soil.
branches.cn: 土地本身有天气、河流与土壤。

branches.en: The same word holds the political nation and the quiet countryside.
branches.cn: 同一个词既装着政治的国家，也装着安静的乡野。

branches.en: Countryside and national land are the same ground seen from two distances.
branches.cn: 乡村与国土，是从两个距离看同一片地。

intro.en: Country is a base noun from Old French, and it builds many compounds with side, man and music.
intro.cn: country 是来自古法语的名词词根，能与 side、man、music 等构成大量复合词。

latinIntro.en: The facing base contra- also appears in contrast, contrary and contradict.
latinIntro.cn: 表示对面的词基 contra- 也出现在 contrast、contrary 与 contradict 中。
